bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第137卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 137
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 137

sentences.zh: 【齊紀三】 起上章敦牂，盡玄黓涒灘，凡三年。

translations.literal: [Qi Records III] Beginning in Shangzhang Dunxiang and ending in Xuanmo Yuantan, three years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Qi Records, Part Three] From the year Shangzhang Dunxiang through Xuanmo Yuantan—a span of three years.

sentences.zh: 世祖武皇帝中永明八年（

translations.literal: Eighth year of Yongming, middle period of Emperor Wu the Founding Ancestor (
translations.idiomatic: Eighth year of Yongming of Emperor Wu of Qi (

sentences.zh: 庚午，公元四九零年）

translations.literal: gengwu, the year 490 CE)
translations.idiomatic: gengwu, A.D. 490)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，詔放隔城俘二千餘人還魏。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, an edict released more than two thousand captives from Gecheng to return to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, the court ordered that more than two thousand prisoners taken at Gecheng be sent back to Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，魏主如方山；

translations.literal: On yichou, the Wei ruler went to Mount Fang;
translations.idiomatic: On the day yichou, the Northern Wei emperor traveled to Mount Fang;

sentences.zh: 二月，辛未，如靈泉；

translations.literal: in the second month, on xinwei, he went to Lingquan;
translations.idiomatic: in the second month, on xinwei, he went to Lingquan;

sentences.zh: 壬申，還宮。

translations.literal: on renshen, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: on renshen, he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 地豆乾頻寇魏邊，夏，四月，甲戌，魏徵西大將軍陽平王頤擊走之。

translations.literal: Didougan repeatedly raided the Wei frontier; in summer, the fourth month, on jiaxu, Wei's General Who Conquers the West, the Prince of Yangping, Yi, drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Didougan raided the Northern Wei border again and again. In summer, the fourth month, on jiaxu, Yi's Prince of Yangping, general who conquered the west, routed him.

sentences.zh: 頤，新城之子也。

translations.literal: Yi was the son of Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was a son of the Prince of Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 甲午，魏遣兼員外散騎常侍邢產等來聘。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Wei sent the acting supernumerary attendant cavalier attendant-in-ordinary Xing Chan and others on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Northern Wei sent Xing Chan, acting supernumerary attendant cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, and others as envoys.

sentences.zh: 五月，己酉，庫莫奚寇魏邊，安州都將樓龍兒擊走之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on jiyou, the Kumo Xi raided the Wei frontier; the commander-in-chief of Anzhou, Lou Long'er, drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on jiyou, the Kumo Xi attacked the Wei border. Lou Long'er, commander-in-chief of Anzhou, repulsed them.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，辛丑，以會稽太守安陸侯緬為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on xinchou, the Marquis of Anlu, Mian, who was governor of Kuaiji, was made governor of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on xinchou, Mian, Marquis of Anlu and governor of Kuaiji, was appointed governor of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 緬，鸞之弟也。

translations.literal: Mian was the younger brother of Luan.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was a younger brother of Emperor Ming (Xiao Luan).

sentences.zh: 緬留心獄訟，得劫，皆赦遣，許以自新，再犯乃加誅；

translations.literal: Mian paid close attention to prison cases and litigation; when bandits were captured, he pardoned and released them all, allowing them to reform—only repeat offenders were punished with death;
translations.idiomatic: Mian took a close interest in criminal cases. When robbers were caught, he pardoned and released them on promise of reform; only those who offended again were put to death;

sentences.zh: 民畏而愛之。

translations.literal: the people feared yet loved him.
translations.idiomatic: the people both feared and loved him.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，大赦。

translations.literal: On guimao, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, the court proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 丙午，魏主如方山；

translations.literal: On bingwu, the Wei ruler went to Mount Fang;
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, the Wei emperor went to Mount Fang;

sentences.zh: 丙辰，遂如靈泉池；

translations.literal: on bingchen, he then went to the Lingquan Pool;
translations.idiomatic: on bingchen, he proceeded to the Lingquan Pool;

sentences.zh: 八月，丙寅朔，還宮。

translations.literal: in the eighth month, on the first day of the cycle bingyin, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: in the eighth month, on the new moon of bingyin, he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 河南王度易侯卒；

translations.literal: The Prince of Henan, Duyihou, died;
translations.idiomatic: Duyihou, Prince of Henan, died;

sentences.zh: 乙酉，以其世子伏連籌為秦、河二州刺史，遣振武將軍丘冠先拜授，且吊之。

translations.literal: on yiyou, his heir Fuliancou was made governor of Qin and He provinces; the General Who Quells Martial Foes, Qiu Guanxian, was sent to invest him with office and also to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: on yiyou, his heir Fuliancou was appointed governor of Qin and He provinces. The general who quells martial foes, Qiu Guanxian, was sent to invest him and offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 伏連籌逼冠先使拜，冠先不從，伏連籌推冠先墜崖而死。

translations.literal: Fuliancou forced Guanxian to perform obeisance; Guanxian refused, and Fuliancou pushed Guanxian off a cliff to his death.
translations.idiomatic: Fuliancou tried to force Guanxian to bow to him. Guanxian refused, and Fuliancou pushed him off a cliff to his death.

sentences.zh: 上厚賜其子雄；

translations.literal: The Emperor richly rewarded Guanxian's son Xiong;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor gave generous rewards to Guanxian's son Xiong;

sentences.zh: 敕以喪委絕域，不可復尋，仕進無嫌。

translations.literal: and ordered that since the bereavement had been entrusted to a remote region and could not be recovered, there should be no objection to Xiong's advancement in office.
translations.idiomatic: and decreed that because the father's body had been lost in a distant land and could not be recovered, there was no bar to the son's pursuing an official career.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史巴東王子響，有勇力，善騎射，好武事，自選帶仗左右六十人，皆有膽干；

translations.literal: The Prince of Badong, Zixiang, who was governor of Jingzhou, was brave and strong, skilled at mounted archery, and fond of military affairs; he personally selected sixty armed attendants, all bold and capable;
translations.idiomatic: Zixiang, Prince of Badong and governor of Jingzhou, was strong and brave, skilled at mounted archery, and devoted to military matters. He personally chose sixty armed retainers, every one bold and capable;

sentences.zh: 至鎮，數於內齋以牛酒犒之。

translations.literal: on reaching his post, he repeatedly entertained them with beef and wine in his private quarters.
translations.idiomatic: once at his post, he often feasted them with beef and wine in his private quarters.

sentences.zh: 又私作錦袍、絳襖，欲以餉蠻，交易器仗。

translations.literal: He also privately had brocade robes and crimson jackets made, intending to present them to the barbarians in exchange for weapons.
translations.idiomatic: He also had brocade robes and crimson jackets made in secret, planning to trade them to the tribal peoples for arms.

sentences.zh: 長史高平劉寅、司馬安定席恭穆等連名密啟。

translations.literal: The chief administrator Liu Yin of Gaoping, the marshal Xi Gongmu of Anding, and others jointly submitted a secret memorial under their names.
translations.idiomatic: The chief administrator Liu Yin of Gaoping, the marshal Xi Gongmu of Anding, and others filed a joint secret report.

sentences.zh: 上敕精檢。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered a thorough investigation.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered a thorough investigation.

sentences.zh: 子響聞台使至不見敕，召寅、恭穆及咨議參軍江悆、典簽吳修之、魏景淵等詰之，寅等秘而不言；

translations.literal: When Zixiang heard that an imperial envoy had arrived but did not see the edict, he summoned Yin, Gongmu, the consulting military adjutant Jiang Yu, the registrar Wu Xiuzhi, Wei Jingyuan, and others to question them; Yin and the others kept the matter secret and would not speak;
translations.idiomatic: Zixiang heard that an imperial envoy had arrived but had not seen the edict. He summoned Yin, Gongmu, the consulting adjutant Jiang Yu, the registrar Wu Xiuzhi, Wei Jingyuan, and others to question them. Yin and his colleagues kept silent;

sentences.zh: 修之曰：「既已降敕，政應方便答塞。」

translations.literal: Xiuzhi said, "Since an edict has already been issued, we ought simply to give a convenient reply to satisfy them."
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi said, "An edict has already been sent down—we should just give them a plausible answer and be done with it."

sentences.zh: 景淵曰：「應先檢校。」

translations.literal: Jingyuan said, "We should first conduct a search and verification."
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan said, "We should search the premises first."

sentences.zh: 子響大怒，執寅等八人，於後堂殺之，具以啟聞。

translations.literal: Zixiang flew into a rage, seized Yin and seven others, and killed them in the rear hall; he reported everything in full to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiang flew into a rage, seized Yin and seven others, and killed them in the rear hall, then reported the whole affair to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上欲赦江悆，聞皆已死，怒。

translations.literal: The Emperor had wished to pardon Jiang Yu, but on hearing that all had already been killed, he was angry.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had intended to pardon Jiang Yu, but when he learned that all eight were already dead, he was furious.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，以隨王子隆為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: On renchen, the Prince of Sui, Zilong, was made governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Zilong, Prince of Sui, was appointed governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 上欲遣淮南太守戴僧靜將兵討子響，僧靜面啟曰：「巴東王年少，長史執之太急，忿不思難故耳。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to send the governor of Huainan, Dai Sengjing, to lead troops against Zixiang. Sengjing addressed him directly, saying, "The Prince of Badong is young; the chief administrator pressed him too hard, and in anger he failed to consider the consequences—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor planned to send Dai Sengjing, governor of Huainan, to lead troops against Zixiang. Sengjing spoke to him in person: "The Prince of Badong is young. The chief administrator pushed him too hard; in a fit of anger he acted without thinking—that is all there is to it.

sentences.zh: 天子兒過誤殺人，有何大罪！

translations.literal: A son of Heaven who kills someone in a moment of error—what great crime is that!
translations.idiomatic: When an emperor's son kills someone in a fit of temper, what grave crime is that?

sentences.zh: 官忽遣軍西上，人情惶懼，無所不至。

translations.literal: If the court suddenly sends an army westward, popular alarm will know no bounds.
translations.idiomatic: If the court suddenly sends troops west, panic will spread everywhere.

sentences.zh: 僧靜不敢奉敕。」

translations.literal: Sengjing dares not accept this commission."
translations.idiomatic: I dare not accept this commission."

sentences.zh: 上不答而心善之。

translations.literal: The Emperor made no reply but inwardly approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor did not answer, but he was pleased at heart.

sentences.zh: 乃遣衛尉胡諧之、游擊將軍尹略、中書舍人茹法亮帥齋仗數百人詣江陵，檢捕群小，敕之曰：「子響若束手自歸，可全其命。」

translations.literal: He then sent the Commandant of the Guards Hu Xiezhi, the mobile corps general Yin Lue, and the palace secretariat attendant Ru Faliang to lead several hundred palace guards to Jiangling to investigate and seize the ringleaders, instructing them: "If Zixiang binds himself and surrenders, his life may be spared."
translations.idiomatic: Instead he sent Hu Xiezhi, commandant of the guards, Yin Lue, mobile corps general, and Ru Faliang, palace secretariat attendant, with several hundred palace guards to Jiangling to round up the ringleaders, with orders: "If Zixiang surrenders with bound hands, his life may be spared."

sentences.zh: 以平南內史張欣泰為諧之副。

translations.literal: Zhang Xintai, interior minister of Pingnan, was made Xiezhi's deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xintai, interior minister of Pingnan, was appointed Xiezhi's deputy.

sentences.zh: 欣泰謂諧之曰：「今段之行，勝既無名，負成奇恥。

translations.literal: Xintai said to Xiezhi, "On this expedition, victory would bring no renown, while defeat would be an extraordinary disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Xintai told Xiezhi, "On this mission, victory would win us no glory, and defeat would be a lasting shame.

sentences.zh: 彼凶狡相聚，所以為其用者，或利賞逼威，無由自潰。

translations.literal: Those fierce and cunning men have gathered together; those who serve them do so either for profit and reward or under coerced authority—they will not disperse on their own.
translations.idiomatic: His fierce followers have banded together. Those who fight for him do so for gain or under duress—they will not melt away on their own.

sentences.zh: 若頓軍夏口，宣示禍福，可不戰而擒也。」

translations.literal: If we halt the army at Xiakou and proclaim fortune and misfortune, we can take him without fighting."
translations.idiomatic: If we halt at Xiakou and make clear what awaits them, we can take him without a battle."

sentences.zh: 諧之不從。

translations.literal: Xiezhi did not follow this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Xiezhi would not listen.

sentences.zh: 欣泰，興世之子也。

translations.literal: Xintai was the son of Xingshi.
translations.idiomatic: Xintai was a son of Zhang Xingshi.

sentences.zh: 諧之等至江津，築城燕尾洲。

translations.literal: Xiezhi and the others reached the ford at the Yangtze and built a fort on Swallowtail Islet.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiezhi and his party reached the Yangtze crossing, they built a fort on Swallowtail Islet.

sentences.zh: 子響白服登城，頻遣使與相聞，曰：「天下豈有兒反！

translations.literal: Zixiang, dressed in white, mounted the wall and repeatedly sent messengers to communicate, saying, "Under heaven, can a son truly be a rebel!
translations.idiomatic: Zixiang, dressed in white, went up on the wall and sent messengers again and again, saying, "Under heaven, can a son truly be called a rebel!

sentences.zh: 身不作賊，直是粗疏。

translations.literal: I am no bandit—only coarse and careless.
translations.idiomatic: I am no traitor—only rash and heedless.

sentences.zh: 今便單舸還闕，受殺人之罪，何築城見捉邪！」

translations.literal: I will now return alone in a single boat to the capital to accept punishment for killing men—why build a fort to capture me!"
translations.idiomatic: I will sail alone back to court to answer for the killings—why must you build a fort to seize me!"

sentences.zh: 尹略獨答曰：「誰將汝反父人共語！」

translations.literal: Yin Lue alone replied, "Who would speak with you, a man who rebels against his father!"
translations.idiomatic: Yin Lue alone answered, "Who would parley with a son who turns against his father!"

sentences.zh: 子響唯灑泣；

translations.literal: Zixiang could only weep;
translations.idiomatic: Zixiang could only weep;

sentences.zh: 乃殺牛，具酒饌，餉台軍，略棄之江流。

translations.literal: he then slaughtered an ox and prepared food and drink to present to the imperial army; Lue threw them into the river.
translations.idiomatic: he had an ox killed and sent food and wine to the imperial troops; Lue threw the gifts into the river.

sentences.zh: 子響呼茹法亮；

translations.literal: Zixiang called for Ru Faliang;
translations.idiomatic: Zixiang called for Ru Faliang;

sentences.zh: 法亮疑畏，不肯往。

translations.literal: Faliang, suspicious and afraid, would not go.
translations.idiomatic: Faliang, fearful and suspicious, refused to go.

sentences.zh: 又求見傳詔；

translations.literal: Zixiang again asked to see the edict-bearer;
translations.idiomatic: Zixiang again asked to see the imperial messenger;

sentences.zh: 法亮亦不遣，且執錄其使。

translations.literal: Faliang would not send him either, and moreover seized and detained Zixiang's messenger.
translations.idiomatic: Faliang would not send anyone and seized Zixiang's messenger besides.

sentences.zh: 子響怒，遣所養勇士收集府、州兵二千人，從靈溪西渡；

translations.literal: Zixiang was enraged and sent the warriors he had raised to gather two thousand prefectural and provincial troops and cross westward from Lingxi;
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Zixiang sent his personal warriors to muster two thousand prefectural and provincial troops and cross the Lingxi westward;

sentences.zh: 子響自與百餘人操萬鈞弩，宿江堤上。

translations.literal: Zixiang himself, with more than a hundred men operating ten-thousand-jin crossbows, camped on the river embankment.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiang himself took more than a hundred men with heavy crossbows and camped on the river bank.

sentences.zh: 明日，府、州兵與台軍戰，子響於堤上發弩射之，台軍大敗；

translations.literal: The next day, the prefectural and provincial troops fought the imperial army; Zixiang shot at them from the embankment with his crossbows, and the imperial army was utterly defeated;
translations.idiomatic: The next day the prefectural and provincial troops fought the imperial force. Zixiang fired his crossbows from the bank, and the imperial army was routed;

sentences.zh: 尹略死，諧之等單艇逃去。

translations.literal: Yin Lue was killed, and Xiezhi and the others escaped in a single small boat.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Lue was killed; Xiezhi and the others fled in a lone skiff.

sentences.zh: 上又遣丹陽尹蕭順之將兵繼至，子響即日將白衣左右三十人，乘舴艋沿流赴建康。

translations.literal: The Emperor again sent the governor of Danyang, Xiao Shunzhi, to lead troops in pursuit; that same day Zixiang took thirty attendants in white and boarded a small boat to go downstream to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Xiao Shunzhi, governor of Danyang, with more troops in pursuit. That same day Zixiang took thirty attendants dressed in white and set out downstream for Jiankang in a small boat.

sentences.zh: 太子長懋素忌子響，順之之發建康也，太子密諭順之，使早為之所，勿令得還。

translations.literal: The crown prince Changmao had long resented Zixiang; when Shunzhi set out from Jiankang, the crown prince secretly instructed him to deal with Zixiang early and not let him return.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Changmao had long envied Zixiang. When Shunzhi left Jiankang, the crown prince secretly told him to settle matters quickly and not let Zixiang reach the capital alive.

sentences.zh: 子響見順之，欲自申明；

translations.literal: When Zixiang met Shunzhi, he wished to explain himself;
translations.idiomatic: When Zixiang met Shunzhi, he tried to plead his case;

sentences.zh: 順之不許，於射堂縊殺之。

translations.literal: Shunzhi would not allow it and strangled him in the archery hall.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzhi would not hear him and strangled him in the archery hall.

sentences.zh: 子響臨死，啟上曰：「臣罪逾山海，分甘斧鉞。

translations.literal: As he faced death, Zixiang addressed the Emperor: "Your servant's crimes exceed mountains and seas; I willingly accept the axe and halberd.
translations.idiomatic: Facing death, Zixiang wrote to the Emperor: "My crimes tower higher than mountains and seas; I accept the axe without complaint.

sentences.zh: 敕遣諧之等至，竟無宣旨，便建旗入津，對城南岸築城守。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty's order sent Xiezhi and the others, they brought no proclamation of the imperial will, but at once raised banners and entered the ford, building a fort on the south bank of the city to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: When you sent Xiezhi and the others, they announced no imperial decree but at once raised banners, entered the crossing, and built a fort on the south bank to besiege me.

sentences.zh: 臣累遣書信呼法亮，乞白服相見；

translations.literal: Your servant repeatedly sent letters summoning Faliang, begging to meet him dressed in white;
translations.idiomatic: I sent letter after letter asking Faliang to come, begging to meet him in white robes;

sentences.zh: 法亮終不肯。

translations.literal: Faliang in the end would not come.
translations.idiomatic: Faliang would not come.

sentences.zh: 群小懼怖，遂致攻戰，此臣之罪也。

translations.literal: The lesser men were afraid, and thus fighting broke out—this is your servant's crime.
translations.idiomatic: My followers panicked, and fighting followed—that is my fault.

sentences.zh: 臣此月二十五日，束身投軍，希還天闕，停宅一月，臣自取盡，可使齊代無殺子之譏，臣免逆父之謗。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fifth of this month your servant bound himself and surrendered to the army, hoping to return to the heavenly court, remain at home one month, and then accept my end—so that the Qi dynasty might be free of the reproach of killing a son, and your servant free of the slander of rebelling against a father.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fifth of this month I surrendered with bound hands, hoping to return to court, stay at home one month, and then accept whatever fate you decree—so that Qi might escape the charge of killing a son, and I the charge of turning against my father.

sentences.zh: 既不遂心，今便命盡。

translations.literal: Since this wish was not granted, I now end my life.
translations.idiomatic: Since that hope was denied, my life ends today.

sentences.zh: 臨啟哽塞，知復何陳！」

translations.literal: As I close this memorial, my throat chokes—what more can I say!"
translations.idiomatic: My throat closes as I write—what more is there to say!"

sentences.zh: 有司奏絕子響屬籍，削爵土，易姓蛸氏；

translations.literal: The responsible officials memorialized to strike Zixiang from the clan register, strip his fief and rank, and change his surname to the Xiao clan;
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials recommended that Zixiang be struck from the imperial clan register, stripped of his title and fief, and given the surname Xiao;

sentences.zh: 諸所連坐，別下考論。

translations.literal: all those implicated were to be dealt with separately according to review.
translations.idiomatic: those implicated were to be tried and punished on their own merits.

sentences.zh: 久之，上游華林園，見一猿透擲悲鳴，問左右，曰：「猿子前日墜崖死。」

translations.literal: After some time, the Emperor went up to the Hualin Garden and saw an ape leaping about and crying mournfully; he asked those beside him, who said, "The ape's young fell from a cliff and died the other day."
translations.idiomatic: Some time later the Emperor visited the Hualin Garden and saw an ape leaping and wailing. When he asked his attendants, they said, "Its young fell from a cliff and died a few days ago."

sentences.zh: 上思子響，因嗚咽流涕。

translations.literal: The Emperor thought of Zixiang and wept aloud.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor thought of Zixiang and broke into sobs.

sentences.zh: 茹法亮頗為上所責怒，蕭順之慚懼，發疾而卒。

translations.literal: Ru Faliang was much blamed and rebuked by the Emperor; Xiao Shunzhi, ashamed and afraid, fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Ru Faliang bore the brunt of the Emperor's anger. Xiao Shunzhi, stricken with shame and fear, fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 豫章王嶷表請收葬子響；

translations.literal: The Prince of Yuzhang, Xiao Li, memorialized requesting permission to gather and bury Zixiang;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Li, Prince of Yuzhang, petitioned to bury Zixiang properly;

sentences.zh: 不許，貶為魚復侯。

translations.literal: permission was not granted; Zixiang was demoted to Marquis of Yufu.
translations.idiomatic: the request was denied, and Zixiang was posthumously demoted to Marquis of Yufu.

sentences.zh: 子響之亂，方鎮皆啟子響為逆，兗州刺史垣榮祖曰：「此非所宜言。

translations.literal: During Zixiang's disturbance, the regional commanders all reported that Zixiang had rebelled; the governor of Yanzhou, Yuan Rongzu, said, "This is not what ought to be said.
translations.idiomatic: During Zixiang's uprising, the regional commanders all reported that he had rebelled. Yuan Rongzu, governor of Yanzhou, said, "That is not what ought to be said.

sentences.zh: 正應云：『劉寅等孤負恩獎，逼迫巴東，使至於此。』」

translations.literal: One should simply say: 'Liu Yin and the others betrayed favor and reward, pressed the Prince of Badong, and brought matters to this pass.'"
translations.idiomatic: The proper report is: 'Liu Yin and the others betrayed imperial favor and drove the Prince of Badong to this extremity.'"

sentences.zh: 上省之，以榮祖為知言。

translations.literal: The Emperor took note of this and considered Rongzu a man of sound judgment.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor noted this and judged Rongzu a man of sense.

sentences.zh: 台軍焚燒江陵府捨，官曹文書，一時蕩盡。

translations.literal: The imperial army burned the prefectural offices at Jiangling; official documents were destroyed at once.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial troops burned the government buildings at Jiangling, and all official records were lost at once.

sentences.zh: 上以大司馬記室南陽樂藹屢為本州僚佐，引見，問以西事。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because the recorder of the Grand Marshal, Yue Ai of Nanyang, had repeatedly served as an official of this province, summoned him for audience and questioned him about western affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yue Ai of Nanyang, recorder in the office of the grand marshal, had served several times in Jingzhou, the Emperor summoned him and questioned him about affairs in the west.

sentences.zh: 藹應對詳敏，上悅，用為荊州治中，敕付以修復府州事。

translations.literal: Ai answered in detail and with alertness; the Emperor was pleased and appointed him administrative aide of Jingzhou, ordering him entrusted with restoring the prefectural and provincial administration.
translations.idiomatic: Ai answered with precision and ease. The Emperor was pleased and appointed him administrative aide of Jingzhou, charging him with rebuilding the provincial government.

sentences.zh: 藹繕修廨捨數百區，頃之鹹畢，而役不及民，荊部稱之。

translations.literal: Ai repaired several hundred office compounds; shortly all were complete, yet the labor did not reach the common people, and the Jing region praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Ai restored several hundred government buildings. Soon all were finished, yet the common people were not pressed into service, and Jingzhou acclaimed him.

sentences.zh: 九月，癸丑，魏太皇太后馮氏殂；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on guichou, the Grand Empress Dowager Feng of Wei died;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on guichou, Grand Empress Dowager Feng of Northern Wei died;

sentences.zh: 高祖勺飲不入口者五日，哀毀過禮。

translations.literal: the High Ancestor took not a spoonful of drink or food for five days, his grief and devastation exceeding the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen took neither food nor drink for five days, mourning beyond what ritual prescribed.

sentences.zh: 中部曹華陰楊椿諫曰：「陛下荷祖宗之業，臨萬國之重，豈可同匹夫之節以取僵仆！

translations.literal: Yang Chun of Huayin in the Central Section memorialized in remonstrance: "Your Majesty bears the enterprise of the ancestors and presides over the weight of ten thousand states—how can you share the conduct of a common man and court collapse!
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chun of Huayin in the central section remonstrated: "Your Majesty bears the legacy of your ancestors and the weight of the realm—how can you follow a commoner's grief to the point of collapse!

sentences.zh: 群下惶灼，莫知所言。

translations.literal: Your officials are anxious and distressed, not knowing what to say.
translations.idiomatic: Your officials are in anguish and do not know what to say.

sentences.zh: 且聖人之禮，毀不滅性；

translations.literal: Moreover, in the rites of the sages, grief does not extinguish one's nature;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the sages taught that mourning must not destroy the living;

sentences.zh: 縱陛下欲自賢於萬代，其若宗廟何！」

translations.literal: even if Your Majesty wishes to surpass all ages in virtue, what of the ancestral temple!"
translations.idiomatic: even if you wish to outshine all ages in filial piety, what of the ancestral shrines!"

sentences.zh: 帝感其言，為之一進粥。

translations.literal: The Emperor was moved by these words and for that reason took one bowl of gruel.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was moved and took a bowl of gruel.

sentences.zh: 於是諸王公等皆詣闕上表，「請時定兆域，及依漢、魏故事，並太皇太后終制，既葬，公除。」

translations.literal: Thereupon the princes and dukes all came to the palace and submitted memorials, "requesting that the burial site be fixed in timely fashion, and that following the precedents of Han and Wei, together with the final rites for the Grand Empress Dowager, once burial is complete, public mourning be ended."
translations.idiomatic: Then the princes and nobles all came to court with memorials, "asking that the burial ground be chosen promptly and that, following Han and Wei precedent and the Grand Empress Dowager's final instructions, public mourning end once the funeral was complete."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「自遭禍罰，慌惚如昨，奉侍梓宮，猶希彷彿。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Since suffering this calamity, I have been dazed as if it were yesterday; attending the coffin, I still hope for a semblance of her presence.
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "Since this blow fell, I have been dazed as if it were yesterday. Attending her coffin, I still half expect to see her.

sentences.zh: 山陵遷厝，所未忍聞。」

translations.literal: The removal of the mountain tomb—I cannot bear to hear of it."
translations.idiomatic: I cannot bear even to hear of moving her to the tomb."

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，王公復上表固請，詔曰：「山陵可依典冊；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, the princes and dukes again submitted memorials firmly requesting; an edict said: "The mountain tomb may follow the canonical regulations;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, the princes and nobles again petitioned insistently. An edict replied: "The burial may follow the canonical regulations;

sentences.zh: 衰服之宜，情所未忍。」

translations.literal: as for putting off mourning garments, my feelings cannot yet bear it."
translations.idiomatic: but to lay aside mourning garments—my heart cannot yet bear that."

sentences.zh: 帝欲親至陵所，戊辰，詔：「諸常從之具，悉可停之；

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to go in person to the tomb site; on wuchen, an edict said: "All the usual retinue and equipage may be halted;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wished to visit the tomb in person. On wuchen he decreed: "All the usual retinue and equipage may be dispensed with;

sentences.zh: 其武衛之官，防侍如法。」

translations.literal: only the military guard officers shall attend for protection according to regulation."
translations.idiomatic: only the military guard shall attend for protection as the law requires."

sentences.zh: 癸酉，葬文明太皇太后於永固陵。

translations.literal: On guiyou, the Civilized Empress Dowager was buried at Yonggu Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, the Civilized Empress Dowager was buried at Yonggu Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，帝謁陵，王公固請公除。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, the Emperor visited the tomb; the princes and dukes again firmly requested that public mourning be ended.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, the Emperor visited the tomb. The princes and nobles again pressed for an end to public mourning.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「比當別敘在心。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "Shortly I shall set forth my thoughts separately."
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "I shall explain my mind in due course."

sentences.zh: 己卯，又謁陵。

translations.literal: On jimao, he again visited the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, he visited the tomb again.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，帝出至思賢門右，與群臣相慰勞。

translations.literal: On gengchen, the Emperor went out to the right of the Sixian Gate and exchanged condolences and encouragement with the assembled ministers.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, the Emperor went out to the right of the Sixian Gate and met with his ministers to offer mutual condolences.

sentences.zh: 太尉丕等進言曰：「臣等以老朽之年，歷奉累聖；

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant Pi and others advanced to speak, saying, "We, in our decrepit old age, have served successive sage rulers;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Pi and others spoke up: "We are old men who have served successive emperors;

sentences.zh: 國家舊事，頗所知聞。

translations.literal: and are fairly well informed about the state's former affairs.
translations.idiomatic: and we know something of the state's former ways.

sentences.zh: 伏惟遠祖有大諱之日，唯侍送梓宮者凶服，左右盡皆從吉；

translations.literal: We reflect that on the day of a great taboo for a remote ancestor, only those attending and escorting the coffin wore mourning; all others on the left and right entirely followed auspicious dress;
translations.idiomatic: When a remote ancestor died, only those escorting the coffin wore mourning; everyone else dressed as usual;

sentences.zh: 四祖三宗，因而無改。

translations.literal: the four ancestors and three founders—thus it remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: and this practice held unchanged through four ancestors and three founders.

sentences.zh: 陛下以至孝之性，哀毀過禮。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, with utmost filial nature, grieves and devastates yourself beyond the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, in supreme filial devotion, mourns beyond what ritual allows.

sentences.zh: 伏聞所御三食不滿半溢，晝夜不釋絰帶。

translations.literal: We have heard that the three meals you take do not fill half a dipper, and day and night you do not remove your hemp mourning sash.
translations.idiomatic: We hear that your three daily meals do not fill half a bowl, and day and night you never remove your mourning sash.

sentences.zh: 臣等叩心絕氣，坐不安席。

translations.literal: We knock our hearts and hold our breath, unable to sit at ease on our mats.
translations.idiomatic: Our hearts are wrung with anguish; we cannot sit at ease.

sentences.zh: 願少抑至慕之情，奉行先朝舊典。」

translations.literal: We wish that you would slightly restrain your utmost longing and follow the former court's old statutes."
translations.idiomatic: We beg you to restrain your grief a little and follow the precedents of former reigns."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「哀毀常事，豈足關言！

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Grief and devastation are ordinary matters—how are they worth bringing up!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Grief is a common thing—why raise it!

sentences.zh: 朝夕食粥，粗可支任，諸公何足憂怖！

translations.literal: Morning and evening I eat gruel; it roughly suffices to sustain me—why should you lords worry and fear!
translations.idiomatic: I take gruel morning and evening; that is enough to sustain me—why should you worry!

sentences.zh: 祖宗情專武略，未修文教；

translations.literal: The ancestors devoted themselves to military strategy and did not cultivate literary culture;
translations.idiomatic: Our ancestors devoted themselves to arms and did not cultivate learning;

sentences.zh: 朕今仰稟聖訓，庶習古道，論時比事，又與先世不同。

translations.literal: I now look up to receive the sage's instruction and hope to study the ancient way; comparing times and weighing affairs, this again differs from former ages.
translations.idiomatic: I now receive her sage instruction and hope to follow the ancient way; but our times differ from those of old.

sentences.zh: 太尉等國老，政之所寄，於典記舊式或所未悉，且可知朕大意。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant and other elders of the state, to whom government is entrusted, may not fully know the old forms in the canonical records—yet you may know my general intent.
translations.idiomatic: You elders of the state, to whom government is entrusted, may not know every old form in the records—yet you may grasp my general intent.

sentences.zh: 其餘古今喪禮，朕且以所懷別問尚書游明根、高閭等，公可聽之。」

translations.literal: As for the rest, ancient and modern mourning rites, I shall separately question the Minister of the Masters You Minggen, Gao Lu, and others on what is in my heart—you may listen."
translations.idiomatic: As for the rest of ancient and modern mourning rites, I shall put my thoughts separately to Ministers You Minggen and Gao Lu—you may listen."

sentences.zh: 帝因謂明根等曰：「聖人制卒哭之禮，授服之變，皆奪情以漸。

translations.literal: The Emperor then said to Minggen and the others, "The sages instituted the rite of ending wailing, the changes in granting mourning garments—all gradually restraining emotion.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then said to Minggen and the others, "The sages devised the rites of ending wailing and changing mourning garments—all to ease grief by degrees.

sentences.zh: 今則旬日之間，言及即吉，特成傷理。」

translations.literal: Now, within a span of ten days, to speak of returning to auspicious dress at once—this especially violates reason and feeling."
translations.idiomatic: Yet within ten days you speak of returning to normal dress—that truly wounds both reason and feeling."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣等伏尋金冊遺旨，逾月而葬，葬而即吉；

translations.literal: They replied, "We humbly trace the testamentary instructions in the golden book: burial after a month, and upon burial, return to auspicious dress at once;
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "We have searched the testamentary instructions in the golden book: burial after a month, and upon burial, return to normal dress at once;

sentences.zh: 故於下葬之初，奏練除之事。」

translations.literal: therefore at the beginning of the lowering of the coffin we memorialized about removing the second-stage mourning."
translations.idiomatic: therefore at the burial we memorialized about ending the second stage of mourning."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕惟中代所以不遂三年之喪，蓋由君上違世，繼主初立，君德未流，臣義不洽，故身襲兗冕，行即位之禮。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "I consider that the middle dynasties did not complete the three-year mourning largely because when the ruler departed the world, the succeeding lord had just been established, royal virtue had not yet spread, and ministerial duty was not yet harmonized—therefore they personally assumed the ceremonial cap and robes and performed the rite of accession.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "I believe the middle dynasties did not observe three-year mourning because when a ruler died, the successor had just taken the throne, his virtue had not yet spread, and his ministers' loyalty was not yet settled—so he donned ceremonial dress and performed the accession rites.

sentences.zh: 朕誠不德，在位過紀，足令億兆知有君矣。

translations.literal: I truly lack virtue, yet I have held the throne beyond a full cycle—enough to let the hundred millions know there is a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: I lack virtue, yet I have reigned beyond a full cycle—enough for the people to know they have a ruler.

sentences.zh: 於此之日而不遂哀慕之心，使情禮俱失，深可痛恨！」

translations.literal: On such a day as this, not to fulfill the heart of grieving longing, letting both feeling and rite be lost—deeply to be regretted and hated!"
translations.idiomatic: At such a time, not to follow my heart of mourning, letting both feeling and ritual be lost—that is deeply to be regretted!"

sentences.zh: 高閭曰：「杜預，晉之碩學，論自古天子無有行三年之喪者，以為漢文之制，暗與古合，雖叔世所行，事可承踵。

translations.literal: Gao Lu said, "Du Yu, a great scholar of Jin, argued that from antiquity no Son of Heaven ever practiced three-year mourning, holding that Emperor Wen of Han's system tacitly accorded with antiquity; though practiced in a declining age, the matter may be followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu said, "Du Yu, a great Jin scholar, argued that no Son of Heaven from antiquity ever observed three-year mourning, and that Emperor Wen of Han's practice tacitly matched the ancients. Though a practice of a declining age, it may be followed.

sentences.zh: 是以臣等心婁心婁干請。」

translations.literal: Therefore we, with hearts knocking, earnestly petition."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore we earnestly petition you again and again."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「竊尋金冊之旨，所以奪臣子之心，令早即吉者，慮廢絕政事故也。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "I privately trace the intent of the golden book: the reason for wresting the hearts of ministers and sons and ordering an early return to auspicious dress is concern lest government affairs be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "I understand the golden book's intent: it wrests ministers' hearts and orders an early return to normal dress for fear that government will be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 群公所請，其志亦然。

translations.literal: The petition of the assembled lords has the same aim.
translations.idiomatic: Your petition has the same aim.

sentences.zh: 朕今仰奉冊令，俯順群心，不敢暗默不言以荒庶政；

translations.literal: I now look up to obey the book's command and bow to follow the group's hearts; I dare not keep silent in the dark and let common government fall into ruin;
translations.idiomatic: I now obey the book and bow to your wishes; I dare not keep silent and let government fall into ruin;

sentences.zh: 唯欲衰麻廢吉禮，朔望盡哀誠，情在可許，故專欲行之。

translations.literal: only I wish to keep hemp mourning and set aside auspicious rites, on the new and full moons exhausting my sincere grief—feeling permits this, and therefore I especially wish to practice it.
translations.idiomatic: only I wish to keep my hemp mourning and set aside auspicious rites, and on the new and full moons pour out my grief—my feeling permits this, and I especially wish to do it.

sentences.zh: 如杜預之論，於孺慕之君，諒闇之主，蓋亦誣矣。」

translations.literal: As for Du Yu's argument, applied to a ruler still yearning like a child, a sovereign in silent mourning—it is surely slander."
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu's argument, applied to a ruler still yearning for his mother, a sovereign in silent mourning—it is surely false."

sentences.zh: 秘書丞李彪曰：「漢明德馬後保養章帝，母子之道，無可間然，及後之崩，葬不淹旬，尋已從吉。

translations.literal: The secretary director Li Biao said, "The Enlightened Virtue Empress Ma of Han nurtured Emperor Zhang; the way of mother and son was without reproach; when the empress died, burial took less than ten days, and soon they returned to auspicious dress.
translations.idiomatic: Secretary Director Li Biao said, "Empress Ma of Han, the Enlightened Virtue, raised Emperor Zhang; their bond as mother and son was beyond reproach. When she died, burial came within ten days, and soon mourning ended.

sentences.zh: 然漢章不受譏，明德不損名。

translations.literal: Yet Emperor Zhang of Han received no censure, and Enlightened Virtue's name was not harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Emperor Zhang was not censured, and the empress's name was not harmed.

sentences.zh: 願陛下遵金冊遺令，割哀從議。」

translations.literal: We wish Your Majesty to follow the golden book's final command and cut short grief to accept our counsel."
translations.idiomatic: We beg Your Majesty to follow the golden book's command and set grief aside to accept our counsel."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕所以眷戀衰絰，不從所議者，實情不能忍，豈徒苟免嗤嫌而已哉！

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "The reason I linger over my hemp mourning sash and do not follow your counsel is truly that my feelings cannot bear it—how could it be merely to escape ridicule and blame!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "The reason I cling to my mourning sash and reject your counsel is that my feelings cannot bear it—not merely to escape ridicule!

sentences.zh: 今奉終儉素，一已仰遵遺冊；

translations.literal: In the funeral observances I have followed frugality and simplicity, fully obeying the testamentary book on that point;
translations.idiomatic: In the funeral I have followed frugality, fully obeying the testament on that point;

sentences.zh: 但痛慕之心，事繫於予，庶聖靈不奪至願耳。」

translations.literal: only the heart of painful longing concerns me alone; I hope the sage spirit will not wrest away my utmost wish."
translations.idiomatic: only my heart of grief is mine alone; I hope her spirit will not deny my deepest wish."

sentences.zh: 高閭曰：「陛下既不除服於上，臣等獨除服於下，則為臣之道不足。

translations.literal: Gao Lu said, "If Your Majesty does not remove mourning garments above while we alone remove them below, then our way as ministers is insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu said, "If Your Majesty does not lay aside mourning while we alone do so, our duty as ministers is unfulfilled.

sentences.zh: 又親御衰麻，復聽朝政，吉凶事雜，臣竊為疑。」

translations.literal: Moreover, you personally wear hemp mourning yet again hear court affairs—auspicious and inauspicious matters mixed; we privately find it doubtful."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, you wear mourning yet attend to court—auspicious and inauspicious matters mixed. We find this troubling."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「先後撫念群下，卿等哀慕，猶不忍除，奈何令朕獨忍之於至親乎！

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "The late empress cared for and thought of the group below; you, in grieving longing, still cannot bear to remove mourning—how can you make me alone bear it toward my closest kin!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "The late empress cared for you all; you, in grief, still cannot lay mourning aside—how can you ask me alone to bear it toward my closest kin!

sentences.zh: 朕今逼於遺冊，唯望至期；

translations.literal: I am now pressed by the testamentary book and can only look to the appointed term;
translations.idiomatic: I am now pressed by the testament and can only wait for the appointed term;

sentences.zh: 雖不盡禮，蘊結差申。

translations.literal: though I do not exhaust the rites, the knot in my breast is somewhat eased.
translations.idiomatic: though I do not fulfill every rite, the knot in my breast is somewhat eased.

sentences.zh: 群臣各以親疏、貴賤、遠近為除服之差，庶幾稍近於古，易行於今。」

translations.literal: Let the assembled ministers each, according to closeness or distance, noble or humble rank, near or far, have differences in removing mourning garments—perhaps this will draw somewhat nearer to antiquity and be easier to practice today."
translations.idiomatic: Let each minister remove mourning according to closeness, rank, and distance—perhaps this will approach antiquity and be practicable today."

sentences.zh: 高閭曰：「昔王孫裸葬，士安去棺，其子皆從而不違。

translations.literal: Gao Lu said, "In old times Wang Sun had a naked burial, and Shi An removed the coffin; their sons all followed and did not disobey.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu said, "Wang Sun was buried naked, and Shi An removed his coffin; their sons obeyed without protest.

sentences.zh: 今親奉遺令而有所不從，臣等所以頻煩干奏。」

translations.literal: Now you personally received the final command yet in some matters do not follow it—this is why we repeatedly trouble you with memorials."
translations.idiomatic: Now you received her final command yet in some matters do not follow it—this is why we petition again and again."

sentences.zh: 李彪曰：「三年不改其父之道，可謂大孝。

translations.literal: Li Biao said, "Not to alter one's father's way for three years may be called great filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Li Biao said, "Not to alter one's father's way for three years—that is great filial piety.

sentences.zh: 今不遵冊令，恐涉改道之嫌。」

translations.literal: Now, not following the book's command, I fear we touch on the suspicion of altering the way."
translations.idiomatic: Not to follow the book's command now may invite the charge of altering her way."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「王孫、士安皆誨子以儉，及其遵也，豈異今日！

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Wang Sun and Shi An both admonished their sons with frugality; when they followed, how was it different from today!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Wang Sun and Shi An both taught their sons frugality; when they obeyed, was that so different from today!

sentences.zh: 改父之道，殆與此殊。

translations.literal: Altering a father's way is nearly a different matter from this.
translations.idiomatic: Altering a father's way is a different matter entirely.

sentences.zh: 縱有所涉，甘受後代之譏，未忍今日之請。」

translations.literal: Even if it touches on that, I willingly accept later generations' ridicule and cannot bear today's petition."
translations.idiomatic: Even if I invite later ridicule, I cannot bear to accept your petition today."

sentences.zh: 群臣又言：「春秋烝嘗，事難廢闕。」

translations.literal: The assembled ministers again said, "The spring and autumn offerings and sacrifices—such matters are hard to abandon or omit."
translations.idiomatic: The ministers again said, "The spring and autumn sacrifices cannot be abandoned."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「自先朝以來，恆有司行事；

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "From former reigns onward, officials have always conducted these affairs;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "From former reigns, officials have always conducted them;

sentences.zh: 朕賴蒙慈訓，常親致敬。

translations.literal: I, relying on her loving instruction, often personally paid respect.
translations.idiomatic: I, blessed with her loving instruction, often attended in person.

sentences.zh: 今昊天降罰，人神喪恃，賴宗廟之靈，亦輟歆祀。

translations.literal: Now Heaven above has sent punishment; men and spirits have lost their support; relying on the ancestral temple's spirit, I also suspend the offerings of enjoyment.
translations.idiomatic: Now Heaven has punished me; men and spirits have lost their support. Even with the ancestral temple's aid, I suspend the offerings.

sentences.zh: 脫行饗薦，恐乖冥旨。」

translations.literal: If I were to perform the feasting and presentation, I fear it would violate the intent in the dark realm."
translations.idiomatic: To perform the feasts now would violate her intent in the realm below."

sentences.zh: 群臣又言：「古者葬而即吉，不必終禮，此乃二漢所以經綸治道，魏、晉所以綱理庶政也。」

translations.literal: The assembled ministers again said, "In antiquity, upon burial one returned to auspicious dress; one need not complete the full rites—this is how the two Han dynasties wove the threads of governance, and how Wei and Jin ordered common administration."
translations.idiomatic: The ministers again said, "In antiquity, mourning ended at burial; the full rites need not be completed. This is how the two Han dynasties governed and how Wei and Jin ordered affairs."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「既葬即吉，蓋季欲多亂，權宜救世耳。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Returning to auspicious dress upon burial was largely because in a decadent age desires multiplied and disorder arose—a temporary measure to save the age.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Ending mourning at burial was largely because in decadent times disorder multiplied—a temporary measure to save the age.

sentences.zh: 二漢之盛，魏、晉之興，豈由簡略喪禮、遺忘仁孝哉！

translations.literal: Was the splendor of the two Han, the rise of Wei and Jin, achieved by simplifying mourning rites and forgetting benevolence and filial piety!
translations.idiomatic: Was the glory of Han, the rise of Wei and Jin, achieved by simplifying mourning and forgetting filial piety!

sentences.zh: 平日之時，公卿每稱當今四海晏然，禮樂日新，可以參美唐、虞，比盛夏、商。

translations.literal: In ordinary times, the lords and ministers often praised that today the four seas are tranquil, rites and music daily renew, and we may rival Tang and Yu, compare with the height of Xia and Shang.
translations.idiomatic: In ordinary times you praised our age as peaceful, our rites and music ever renewed, rivaling Tang and Yu and the height of Xia and Shang.

sentences.zh: 及至今日，即欲苦奪朕志，使不逾於魏、晉。

translations.literal: Yet when it comes to today, you at once wish bitterly to wrest my resolve and make me no better than Wei and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Yet today you would bitterly wrest my resolve and make me no better than Wei and Jin.

sentences.zh: 如此之意，未解所由。」

translations.literal: Such intent—I do not understand its origin."
translations.idiomatic: I do not understand this change of heart."

sentences.zh: 李彪曰：「今雖治化清晏，然江南有未賓之吳，漠北有不臣之虜，是以臣等猶懷不虞之慮。」

translations.literal: Li Biao said, "Though governance and transformation are clear and tranquil, south of the Yangtze there is unsubmissive Wu, and north of the desert there are un-submissive barbarians—therefore we still harbor concerns of the unforeseen."
translations.idiomatic: Li Biao said, "Though the realm is at peace, Wu in the south has not submitted, and barbarians in the north have not bowed—therefore we still fear the unforeseen."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「魯公帶絰從戎，晉侯墨衰敗敵，固聖賢所許。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "The Duke of Lu wore his mourning sash and followed the army; the Marquis of Jin wore ink-stained mourning and defeated the enemy—surely the sages permitted this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "The Duke of Lu went to war in his mourning sash; the Marquis of Jin defeated his enemy in ink-stained mourning—the sages permitted this.

sentences.zh: 如有不虞，雖越紼無嫌，而況衰麻乎！

translations.literal: If the unforeseen should come, even crossing the coffin ropes would be without blame—how much more so wearing hemp mourning!
translations.idiomatic: If crisis comes, even stepping over the coffin ropes would be blameless—how much more wearing mourning!

sentences.zh: 豈可於晏安之辰豫念軍旅之事，以廢喪紀哉！

translations.literal: How can one, in days of peace and security, premeditate military affairs and thereby abandon mourning observances!
translations.idiomatic: How can one, in days of peace, dwell on military matters and abandon mourning observances!

sentences.zh: 古人亦有稱王者除衰而諒闇終喪者，若不許朕衰服，則當除衰拱默，委政塚宰。

translations.literal: The ancients also spoke of kings who removed mourning garments yet in silent obscurity completed the mourning—if you do not permit me hemp mourning, then I should remove mourning, fold my hands in silence, and entrust government to the chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients also spoke of kings who laid aside mourning yet completed it in silent seclusion. If you will not let me wear mourning, I shall lay it aside, hold my peace, and entrust government to the chief minister.

sentences.zh: 二事之中，唯公卿所擇。」

translations.literal: Between these two courses, let the lords and ministers choose."
translations.idiomatic: Between these two courses, choose."

sentences.zh: 游明根曰：「淵默不言，則不政將曠；

translations.literal: You Minggen said, "Deep silence without speech, and government will fall idle;
translations.idiomatic: You Minggen said, "Deep silence, and government will fall idle;

sentences.zh: 仰順聖心，請從衰服。」

translations.literal: looking up to follow the sage heart, we request that you keep hemp mourning."
translations.idiomatic: bowing to your sacred will, we ask that you keep your mourning garments."

sentences.zh: 太尉丕曰：「臣與尉元歷事五帝，魏家故事，尤諱之後三月，必迎神於西，禳惡於北，具行吉禮，自皇始以來，未之或改。」

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant Pi said, "Your servant and Yuanyuan have served five emperors; in Wei family precedent, three months after a great taboo one must welcome the spirit in the west and expel evil in the north, fully performing auspicious rites—from Huangshi onward, this has never been altered."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Pi said, "Yuanyuan and I have served five emperors. In Wei custom, three months after a great taboo the spirit must be welcomed in the west and evil expelled in the north, with full auspicious rites—from Huangshi onward, this has never changed."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「若能以道事神，不迎自至；

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "If one can serve the spirits with the Way, without welcoming they come of themselves;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "If one serves the spirits with the Way, they come without being summoned;

sentences.zh: 苟失仁義，雖迎不來。

translations.literal: if one lacks benevolence and righteousness, though one welcomes, they do not come.
translations.idiomatic: if one lacks benevolence and righteousness, they will not come though summoned.

sentences.zh: 此乃平日所不當行，況吾喪乎！

translations.literal: This is what ought not to be done in ordinary times—how much more in my mourning!
translations.idiomatic: This ought not be done in ordinary times—how much more in my mourning!

sentences.zh: 朕在不言之地，不應如此喋喋；

translations.literal: I am in the place of not speaking and ought not to be so talkative;
translations.idiomatic: I am in the place of silence and ought not to be so talkative;

sentences.zh: 但公卿執奪朕情，遂成往復，追用悲絕。」

translations.literal: but the lords and ministers insist on wresting my feelings, and thus this back-and-forth arises, recalling grief to the breaking point."
translations.idiomatic: but you insist on wresting my feelings, and this back-and-forth recalls grief to the breaking point."

sentences.zh: 遂號慟，群官亦哭而辭出。

translations.literal: He then wailed aloud; the assembled officials also wept and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He then wailed aloud; the officials wept and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 初，太后忌帝英敏，恐不利於己，欲廢之，盛寒，閉於空室，絕其食三日；

translations.literal: Earlier, the empress dowager resented the Emperor's keen intelligence, fearing it would not benefit her, and wished to depose him; in severe cold she shut him in an empty room and cut off his food for three days;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the empress dowager resented the Emperor's keen intelligence and feared it would harm her. She wished to depose him. In severe cold she shut him in an empty room and cut off his food for three days;

sentences.zh: 召咸陽王禧，將立之。

translations.literal: she summoned the Prince of Xianyang, Xi, intending to establish him.
translations.idiomatic: she summoned Xi, Prince of Xianyang, intending to make him emperor.

sentences.zh: 太尉東陽王丕、尚書右僕射穆泰、尚書李沖固諫，乃止。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant, the Prince of Dongyang, Pi, the Right Vice Director of the Masters Mu Tai, and the Minister Li Chong firmly remonstrated, and she stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Pi, Prince of Dongyang, Vice Director Mu Tai, and Minister Li Chong firmly remonstrated, and she desisted.

sentences.zh: 帝初無憾意，唯深德丕等。

translations.literal: The Emperor at first harbored no resentment, but deeply owed gratitude to Pi and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor at first bore no resentment, but deeply owed gratitude to Pi and the others.

sentences.zh: 泰，崇之玄孫也。

translations.literal: Tai was the great-great-grandson of Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Tai was a great-great-grandson of Mu Chong.

sentences.zh: 又有宦者譖帝於太后，太后杖帝數十；

translations.literal: Moreover, a eunuch slandered the Emperor to the empress dowager, and the empress dowager beat the Emperor several tens of blows;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, a eunuch slandered the Emperor to the empress dowager, and she beat him several dozen times;

sentences.zh: 帝默然受之，不自申理；

translations.literal: the Emperor silently accepted it and did not plead his own case;
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor silently accepted it and made no defense;

sentences.zh: 及太后殂，亦不復追問。

translations.literal: when the empress dowager died, he also did not pursue the matter afterward.
translations.idiomatic: when she died, he did not pursue the matter afterward.

sentences.zh: 甲申，魏主謁永固陵。

translations.literal: On jiashen, the Wei ruler visited Yonggu Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, the Wei emperor visited Yonggu Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，詔曰：「群官以萬機事重，屢求聽政。

translations.literal: On xinmao, an edict said, "The assembled officials, because the myriad affairs of state are weighty, have repeatedly requested that I hear government.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, an edict said, "The officials, because state affairs are weighty, have repeatedly asked me to hear government.

sentences.zh: 但哀慕纏綿，未堪自力。

translations.literal: But grieving longing entwines me, and I am not yet able to exert myself.
translations.idiomatic: But grief entwines me, and I am not yet able to exert myself.

sentences.zh: 近侍先掌機衡者，皆謀猷所寄，且可委之；

translations.literal: Those close attendants who formerly held the pivots of power—all are entrusted with counsel and may be commissioned for now;
translations.idiomatic: Those close attendants who formerly held power are entrusted with counsel and may be commissioned for now;

sentences.zh: 如有疑事，當時與論決。」

translations.literal: if there are doubtful matters, I shall discuss and decide them at the time."
translations.idiomatic: if doubtful matters arise, I shall discuss and decide them at the time."

sentences.zh: 交州刺史清河房法乘，專好讀書，常屬疾不治事，由是長史伏登之得擅權，改易將吏，不令法乘知。

translations.literal: The governor of Jiaozhou, Fang Fasheng of Qinghe, devoted himself solely to reading books and often claimed illness and did not attend to affairs; thereby the chief administrator Fu Dengzhi was able to monopolize power, changing and replacing generals and officials without letting Fasheng know.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Fasheng of Qinghe, governor of Jiaozhou, devoted himself to reading and often claimed illness, neglecting his duties. Thereby Chief Administrator Fu Dengzhi seized power, changing generals and officials without Fasheng's knowledge.

sentences.zh: 錄事房季文白之，法乘大怒，系登之於獄十餘日。

translations.literal: The recorder Fang Jiwen reported this to him; Fasheng was greatly angered and imprisoned Dengzhi for more than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Recorder Fang Jiwen reported this. Fasheng was furious and imprisoned Dengzhi for more than ten days.

sentences.zh: 登之厚賂法乘妹夫崔景叔，得出，因將部曲襲州，執法乘，謂之曰：「使君既有疾，不宜煩勞。」

translations.literal: Dengzhi richly bribed Fasheng's brother-in-law Cui Jingshu and was released; he then led his troops in a surprise attack on the province, seized Fasheng, and said to him, "Since the governor has illness, he ought not be troubled with vexation."
translations.idiomatic: Dengzhi richly bribed Fasheng's brother-in-law Cui Jingshu and was released. He then led his troops in a surprise attack on the province, seized Fasheng, and said, "Since you are ill, Governor, you ought not be troubled with vexation."

sentences.zh: 囚之別室。

translations.literal: He imprisoned him in a separate room.
translations.idiomatic: He confined him to a separate room.

sentences.zh: 法乘無事，復就登之求書讀之，登之曰：「使君靜處，猶恐動疾，豈可看書！」

translations.literal: Fasheng having nothing to do, again went to Dengzhi to request books to read; Dengzhi said, "Even with the governor resting quietly, I still fear his illness may flare up — how could he read books!"
translations.idiomatic: With nothing else to do, Fasheng again went to Dengzhi to ask for books to read. Dengzhi said, "Even if you rest quietly, Governor, I still fear your illness may worsen — how can you read books!"

sentences.zh: 遂不與。

translations.literal: He then did not give them to him.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to give them to him.

sentences.zh: 乃啟法乘心疾動，不任視事。

translations.literal: He then reported that Fasheng's heart disease had flared up and that he was unfit to attend to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He then reported that Fasheng's heart ailment had worsened and that he was unfit to govern.

sentences.zh: 十一月，乙卯，以登之為交州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on yimao, Dengzhi was appointed governor of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the day yimao, Dengzhi was made governor of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 法乘還，至嶺而卒。

translations.literal: Fasheng returned and died upon reaching the mountain pass.
translations.idiomatic: Fasheng was sent home and died on the road when he reached the pass.

sentences.zh: 十二月，己卯，立皇子子建為湘東王。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on jimao, the emperor's son Zijian was enfeoffed as Prince of Xiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day jimao, the emperor's son Zijian was enfeoffed as Prince of Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖以南方錢少，更欲鑄錢。

translations.literal: Previously, because coin was scarce in the south, the Founding Emperor wished again to cast coin.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, because the south had too little coin in circulation, Emperor Gao wanted to mint more.

sentences.zh: 建元末，奉朝請孔覬上言，以為：「食貨相通，理勢自然。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jianyuan era, Attendant-in-Regular-Audience Kong Xi submitted a memorial, stating, "Food and currency circulate together — this is the natural logic of things.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Jianyuan era, Attendant-in-Regular-Audience Kong Xi submitted a memorial arguing that "food and money must circulate together, as nature and reason require.

sentences.zh: 李悝云：『糴甚貴傷民，甚賤傷農。』

translations.literal: Li Kui said, 'When grain prices are too high it harms the people; when too low it harms the farmers.'
translations.idiomatic: Li Kui said, 'When grain is too dear it hurts the people; when it is too cheap it hurts the farmers.'

sentences.zh: 甚賤甚貴，其傷一也。

translations.literal: Whether too cheap or too dear, the harm is one and the same.
translations.idiomatic: Whether prices are too low or too high, the damage is the same.

sentences.zh: 三吳，國之關奧，比歲時被水潦而糴不貴，是天下錢少，非谷賤，此不可不察也。

translations.literal: The Three Wus are the nation's vital artery; in recent years they have suffered flooding yet grain prices have not risen — this shows that coin is scarce throughout the realm, not that grain is cheap. This must not go unexamined.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Wus are the country's economic heartland. In recent years they have suffered floods, yet grain prices have not risen. That shows coin is scarce across the realm, not that grain is cheap — and this must be understood.

sentences.zh: 鑄錢之弊，在輕重屢變。

translations.literal: The flaw in minting coin lies in the weight and fineness changing repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: The trouble with minting coin is that its weight and value keep changing.

sentences.zh: 重錢患難用，而難用為累輕；

translations.literal: Heavy coin risks being hard to use, and difficulty of use leads toward making it lighter;
translations.idiomatic: Heavy coin is awkward to use, and awkwardness pushes people toward lighter coin;

sentences.zh: 輕錢弊盜鑄，而盜鑄為禍深。

translations.literal: light coin invites illicit casting, and illicit casting brings deep calamity.
translations.idiomatic: light coin invites counterfeiting, and counterfeiting brings deep disaster.

sentences.zh: 民所以盜鑄，嚴法不能禁者，由上鑄錢惜銅愛工也。

translations.literal: The reason the people illicitly cast coin despite harsh laws is that the government, when minting, scrimps on copper and workmanship.
translations.idiomatic: The people counterfeit coin because the state, when minting, scrimps on copper and labor — and harsh laws cannot stop them.

sentences.zh: 惜銅愛工者，意謂錢為無用之器，以通交易，務欲令質輕而數多，使省工而易成，不詳慮其為患也。

translations.literal: Those who scrimp on copper and workmanship think of coin as a useless instrument merely to facilitate trade, striving to make it light in substance and numerous in count, saving labor to make it easy to produce, without carefully considering the harm.
translations.idiomatic: Those who scrimp on copper and labor treat coin as a mere tool for exchange, trying to make it light and plentiful, cheap and easy to produce, without thinking through the harm.

sentences.zh: 夫民之趨利，如水走下。

translations.literal: For the people to pursue profit is like water flowing downhill.
translations.idiomatic: The people chase profit the way water runs downhill.

sentences.zh: 今開其利端，從以重刑，是導其為非而陷之於死，豈為政歟！

translations.literal: Now to open a profit avenue for them and then follow with heavy punishment — this is to lead them into wrongdoing and trap them in death. Is this governance!
translations.idiomatic: To open a path to profit and then punish them severely is to lure people into crime and drive them toward death. Is that how a government should act?

sentences.zh: 漢興，鑄輕錢，民巧偽者多。

translations.literal: When Han rose, it cast light coin, and many among the people practiced fraud.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han dynasty began, it minted light coin, and many people turned to forgery.

sentences.zh: 至元狩中，始懲其弊，乃鑄五銖錢，周郭其上下，令不可磨取鋊，而民計其費不能相償，私鑄益少，此不惜銅不愛工之效也。

translations.literal: By the Yuanshou era they began to redress the flaw, casting the five-zhu coin with rims above and below so the alloy could not be filed off; when the people calculated the cost they could not recoup it, and private casting grew ever less — this is the effect of not scrimping on copper or workmanship.
translations.idiomatic: By the Yuanshou period the court corrected the abuse, minting five-zhu coins with raised rims above and below so the alloy could not be shaved off. When people reckoned the cost, they could not turn a profit, and private minting declined — that is what comes of not scrimping on copper or labor.

sentences.zh: 王者不患無銅乏工，每令民不能競，則盜鑄絕矣。

translations.literal: A sovereign need not worry about lacking copper or labor; whenever the people cannot compete, illicit casting ceases.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler need not fear a shortage of copper or craftsmen. Make it impossible for the people to compete, and counterfeiting will stop.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝鑄四銖，至景和，錢益輕，雖有周郭，而鎔冶不精，於是盜鑄紛紜而起，不可復禁。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Song cast four-zhu coin; by the Jinghe era the coin grew ever lighter; though it had rims, the smelting and casting were not refined, and so illicit casting sprang up in confusion and could no longer be forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Song minted four-zhu coins, but by the Jinghe era the coin had grown lighter still. Though the coins had rims, the smelting was poor, and counterfeiting spread until it could no longer be suppressed.

sentences.zh: 此惜銅愛工之驗也。

translations.literal: This is proof of scrimping on copper and workmanship.
translations.idiomatic: That is the proof of scrimping on copper and labor.

sentences.zh: 凡鑄錢，與其不衷，寧重無輕。

translations.literal: In minting coin generally, rather than miss the middle mark, better heavy than light.
translations.idiomatic: In minting coin, if the weight cannot be exact, better too heavy than too light.

sentences.zh: 自漢鑄五銖至宋文帝，歷五百餘年，制度世有廢興，而不變五銖者明其輕重可法、得貨之宜故也。

translations.literal: From Han's casting of the five-zhu down to Emperor Wen of Song, more than five hundred years passed; institutions rose and fell through the ages, yet the five-zhu did not change — showing that its weight was fit to serve as standard and suited to commerce.
translations.idiomatic: From the Han minting of the five-zhu down to Emperor Wen of Song, more than five hundred years passed. Institutions rose and fell, yet the five-zhu endured because its weight was a reliable standard and suited to trade.

sentences.zh: 案今錢文率皆五銖，異錢時有耳。

translations.literal: Examining present coin, the inscriptions are mostly all five-zhu; variant coin appears only occasionally.
translations.idiomatic: Look at the coin in circulation today: nearly all bear the five-zhu mark; other types appear only now and then.

sentences.zh: 自文帝鑄四銖，又不禁民翦鑿，為禍既博，鐘弊於今，豈不悲哉！

translations.literal: Since Emperor Wen cast the four-zhu and did not forbid the people from clipping and chiseling coin, the harm has been broad; the abuse has culminated in today's ruin — is it not lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Since Emperor Wen minted the four-zhu and failed to forbid clipping and chiseling, the damage has been vast and the abuse has reached today's crisis. Is it not lamentable!

sentences.zh: 晉氏不鑄錢，後經寇戎水火，耗散沈鑠，所失歲多，譬猶磨礱砥礪，不見其損，有時而盡，天下錢何得不竭！

translations.literal: The Jin did not cast coin; afterward through raids, warfare, fire, and flood, coin was wasted, scattered, lost, and melted away — yearly losses were great. It is like grinding on a whetstone: one does not see the wear, but in time it is exhausted. How could coin throughout the realm fail to be depleted!
translations.idiomatic: The Jin stopped minting coin. Afterward, through invasion, war, fire, and flood, coin was wasted, scattered, lost, and melted away year after year. It is like a whetstone worn down by grinding: the loss is invisible until nothing remains. How could the realm's supply of coin fail to run dry!

sentences.zh: 錢竭則士、農、工、商皆喪其業，民何以自存！

translations.literal: When coin is exhausted, scholars, farmers, artisans, and merchants all lose their livelihoods — how can the people sustain themselves!
translations.idiomatic: When coin runs out, scholars, farmers, artisans, and merchants all lose their livelihoods. How can the people survive!

sentences.zh: 愚以為宜如舊制，大興鎔鑄，錢重五銖，一依漢法。

translations.literal: I deem it fit to restore the old system, greatly expand smelting and casting, coin of five-zhu weight, following the Han method entirely.
translations.idiomatic: I believe the state should restore the old system, greatly expand minting, and issue five-zhu coin according to the Han standard.

sentences.zh: 若官鑄者已佈於民，便嚴斷翦鑿，輕小破缺無周郭者，悉不得行。

translations.literal: If officially cast coin has already circulated among the people, then strictly forbid clipping and chiseling; all light, small, broken, or rimless pieces must not circulate.
translations.idiomatic: Once official coin is in circulation among the people, clipping and chiseling must be strictly forbidden, and all light, small, broken, or rimless pieces must be withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 官錢細小者，稱合銖兩，銷以為大，利貧良之民，塞奸巧之路。

translations.literal: Official coin that is small and fine should be weighed to tally with zhu and liang, melted down into large pieces — benefiting the poor and the honest, blocking the path of the crafty.
translations.idiomatic: Small official coin should be weighed to the proper zhu and liang, then melted and recast into full-weight pieces. That would help the poor and honest and shut off the path of fraud.

sentences.zh: 錢貨既均，遠近若一，百姓樂業，市道無爭，衣食滋殖矣。」

translations.literal: Once currency is even, near and far as one, the people will be content in their trades, markets free of strife, and food and clothing will flourish."
translations.idiomatic: Once currency is uniform, near and far alike, the people will prosper in their trades, markets will be free of dispute, and food and clothing will increase."

sentences.zh: 太祖然之，使諸州郡大市銅炭。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor approved this and ordered the major markets of all provinces and commanderies to stock copper and charcoal.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao agreed and ordered the major markets of every province and commandery to gather copper and charcoal.

sentences.zh: 會晏駕，事寢。

translations.literal: Just then the emperor died suddenly and the matter lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: But the emperor died suddenly, and the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 是歲，益州行事劉悛上言：「蒙山下有嚴道銅山，舊鑄錢處，可以經略。」

translations.literal: That year, Acting Governor of Yizhou Liu Quan submitted a memorial, stating, "Under Mount Meng is the copper mountain of Yandao, an old mint site — it can be developed."
translations.idiomatic: That year, Liu Quan, acting governor of Yizhou, submitted a memorial saying, "Beneath Mount Meng lay the copper mountain of Yandao, an old mint site that could be put to use."

sentences.zh: 上從之，遣使入蜀鑄錢。

translations.literal: The emperor consented and sent envoys into Shu to cast coin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and sent envoys into Shu to mint coin.

sentences.zh: 頃之，以功費多而止。

translations.literal: Before long it was halted because costs were too high.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the project was stopped because the expense was too great.

sentences.zh: 自太祖治黃籍，至上，謫巧者戍緣淮各十年，百姓怨望。

translations.literal: Since the Founding Emperor regulated the Yellow Registers, down to the present emperor, those convicted of fraud were penalized to garrison duty along the Huai for ten years each — the people resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Since Emperor Gao reformed the Yellow Registers, the present emperor had punished those guilty of registry fraud with ten years of garrison duty along the Huai frontier, and the people resented it.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔：「自宋升明以前，皆聽復注；

translations.literal: An edict was issued: "For cases before Shengming of Song, all are permitted to be re-registered;
translations.idiomatic: He then issued an edict: "For cases dating before the Shengming era of Song, all may be re-registered;

sentences.zh: 其有謫役邊疆，各許還本；

translations.literal: those who were penalized to frontier service are all permitted to return home;
translations.idiomatic: those sent to frontier service may all return home;

sentences.zh: 此後有犯，嚴加翦治。」

translations.literal: after this, offenders will be strictly punished."
translations.idiomatic: after this, offenders will be punished severely."

sentences.zh: 長沙威王晃卒。

translations.literal: Prince Wei of Changsha, Huang, died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wei of Changsha, Huang, died.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書王晏陳疾自解，上欲以古昌侯鸞代晏領先，手敕問之。

translations.literal: Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Wang Yan cited illness and resigned; the emperor wished to have Marquis of Guchang Luan replace Yan to lead the ministry first, and sent a handwritten edict asking him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan, minister of the Ministry of Personnel, cited illness and resigned. The emperor wanted Marquis of Guchang Luan to take over the ministry first and sent a handwritten edict to ask Yan's view.

sentences.zh: 晏啟曰：「鸞清干有餘；

translations.literal: Yan replied, "Luan has ample integrity and competence;
translations.idiomatic: Yan replied, "Luan has more than enough integrity and ability;

sentences.zh: 然不諳百氏，恐不可居此職。」

translations.literal: yet he is not versed in the hundred schools — I fear he cannot hold this post."
translations.idiomatic: but he is not versed in the hundred schools of thought, and I fear he is not fit for this office."

sentences.zh: 上乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dropped the idea.

sentences.zh: 以百濟王牟大為鎮東大將軍、百濟王。

translations.literal: Mok Da, king of Baekje, was appointed General Who Guards the East and King of Baekje.
translations.idiomatic: Mok Da, king of Baekje, was appointed General Who Guards the East and confirmed as king of Baekje.

sentences.zh: 高車阿伏至羅及窮奇遣使如魏，請為天子討除蠕蠕，魏主賜以繡褲褶及雜彩百匹。

translations.literal: Avuzhiluo and Qiongqi of the Gaoche sent envoys to Wei, asking the Son of Heaven to strike down the Rouran; the Wei ruler granted them embroidered trousers and jacket plus a hundred bolts of assorted silks.
translations.idiomatic: Avuzhiluo and Qiongqi of the Gaoche sent envoys to Wei asking the Son of Heaven to destroy the Rouran. The Wei ruler granted them embroidered trousers and jacket, along with a hundred bolts of assorted silks.

sentences.zh: 世祖武皇帝中永明九年（

translations.literal: Ninth year of Yongming, middle period of Emperor Wu the Founding Ancestor (
translations.idiomatic: Ninth year of Yongming of Emperor Wu of Qi (

sentences.zh: 辛未，公元四九一年）

translations.literal: xinwei, the year 491 CE)
translations.idiomatic: xinwei, A.D. 491)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛丑，上祀南郊。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on xinchou, the emperor sacrificed at the Southern Altars.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the day xinchou, the emperor sacrificed at the Southern Altars.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，魏主始聽政於皇信東室。

translations.literal: On dingmao, the Wei ruler began to hold court in the Eastern Hall of Imperial Trust.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingmao, the Wei ruler began to hold court in the Eastern Hall of Imperial Trust.

sentences.zh: 詔太廟四時之祭：薦宣皇帝，起麵餅、鴨□鶴；

translations.literal: An edict on the seasonal sacrifices at the Grand Temple: for Emperor Xuan, offerings of raised flour cakes, duck and crane;
translations.idiomatic: An edict prescribed the seasonal sacrifices at the Grand Temple: for Emperor Xuan, raised flour cakes, duck and crane offerings;

sentences.zh: 孝皇后，筍、鴨卵；

translations.literal: Empress Xiao: bamboo shoots and duck eggs;
translations.idiomatic: for Empress Xiao, bamboo shoots and duck eggs;

sentences.zh: 高皇帝，肉膾、菹羹；

translations.literal: Emperor Gao: minced meat and pickled-vegetable soup;
translations.idiomatic: for Emperor Gao, minced meat and pickled-vegetable soup;

sentences.zh: 昭皇后，茗、粣、炙魚：皆所嗜也。

translations.literal: Empress Zhao: tea, zha cakes, and broiled fish — all foods they favored.
translations.idiomatic: for Empress Zhao, tea, sacrificial cakes, and broiled fish — all foods they had loved.

sentences.zh: 上夢太祖謂己：「宋氏諸帝常在太廟從我求食，可別為吾致祠。」

translations.literal: The emperor dreamed that the Founding Emperor said to him, "The emperors of Song are always in the Grand Temple begging food from me — you should set up separate rites for me."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dreamed that Emperor Gao said to him, "The Song emperors are always in the Grand Temple begging me for food. You should set up separate rites on my behalf."

sentences.zh: 乃命豫章王妃庾氏四時祠二帝、二後於清溪故宅。

translations.literal: He then ordered Lady Yu, consort of the Prince of Yuzhang, to conduct seasonal sacrifices to the two emperors and two empresses at the old residence at Qingxi.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Lady Yu, consort of the Prince of Yuzhang, to perform seasonal sacrifices to the two emperors and two empresses at the old residence at Qingxi.

sentences.zh: 牲牢、服章，皆用家人禮。

translations.literal: Sacrificial animals and ritual garb all followed household custom.
translations.idiomatic: The sacrificial animals and ritual dress all followed household custom.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：「昔屈到嗜芰，屈建去之，以為不可以私慾干國之典，況子為天子，而以庶人之禮祭其父，違禮甚矣！
