translations.literal: Your subject Guang says, "Long ago Qu Dao loved water chestnuts; Qu Jian removed them, holding that private desire must not interfere with the state's rites — how much more when a son as Son of Heaven uses commoner's rites to sacrifice to his father — a grave breach of ritual!
translations.idiomatic: Your subject Guang says: "Long ago Qu Dao loved water chestnuts, and Qu Jian had them removed, believing private appetite must not interfere with the state's rites. How much worse, then, for a son who is Son of Heaven to sacrifice to his father with the rites of a commoner — a grave breach of ritual!

sentences.zh: 衛成公欲祀相，寧武子猶非之；

translations.literal: When Duke Cheng of Wei wished to sacrifice to Xian, Ning Wuzi still criticized him;
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Cheng of Wei wished to sacrifice to Xian, Ning Wuzi still condemned it;

sentences.zh: 而況降祀祖考於私室，使庶婦屍之乎！」

translations.literal: and how much more to demote sacrifice to one's ancestors to a private chamber and have a commoner's wife preside over it!"
translations.idiomatic: and how much worse to demote sacrifice to one's ancestors to a private house and put a commoner's wife in charge of the rites!"

sentences.zh: 初，魏主召吐谷渾王伏連籌入朝，伏連籌辭疾不至，輒修洮陽、泥和二城，置戍兵焉。

translations.literal: Previously, the Wei ruler summoned Foulianchou, king of Tuyuhun, to court; Foulianchou pleaded illness and did not come, but instead repaired the two cities of Taoyang and Nihe and stationed garrison troops there.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Wei ruler had summoned Foulianchou, king of Tuyuhun, to court. Foulianchou pleaded illness and stayed away, but instead repaired the cities of Taoyang and Nihe and posted garrison troops there.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙亥，魏枹罕鎮將長孫百年請擊二戍，魏主許之。

translations.literal: In the second month, on yihai, Zhangsun Bainian, garrison commander of Baohan in Wei, requested to attack the two garrisons, and the Wei ruler approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day yihai, Zhangsun Bainian, garrison commander of Baohan, asked permission to attack the two outposts, and the Wei ruler agreed.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍裴昭明、散騎侍郎謝竣如魏吊，欲以朝服行事。

translations.literal: Regular Attendant-in-Chamber Pei Zhaoming and Attendant-in-Chamber Xie Jun went to Wei to offer condolences, wishing to perform their mission in court dress.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zhaoming, regular attendant-in-chamber, and Xie Jun, attendant-in-chamber, went to Wei to offer condolences and intended to carry out their mission in court dress.

sentences.zh: 魏主客曰：「吊有常禮，何得以朱衣入凶庭！」

translations.literal: The Wei chief of protocol said, "Condolence rites have fixed norms — how can you enter the hall of mourning in vermilion robes!"
translations.idiomatic: The Wei chief of protocol said, "Condolence visits have fixed rites. How can you enter the mourning hall in vermilion court dress!"

sentences.zh: 昭明等曰：「受命本朝，不敢輒易。」

translations.literal: Zhaoming and the others said, "We received our orders from our court and dare not change them lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoming and the others replied, "We received our orders from our own court and dare not change our dress on our own authority."

sentences.zh: 往返數四，昭明等固執不可。

translations.literal: Back and forth four times, Zhaoming and the others steadfastly refused.
translations.idiomatic: They went back and forth four times, and Zhaoming and the others would not yield.

sentences.zh: 魏主命尚書李沖選學識之士與之言，沖奏遣著作郎上谷成淹。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler ordered Minister Li Chong to select a man of learning to speak with them; Chong memorialized that he would send Compiler Cheng Yan of Shanggu.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei ruler ordered Minister Li Chong to choose a learned man to debate with them. Chong memorialized that he would send Cheng Yan of Shanggu, a compiler at court.

sentences.zh: 昭明等曰：「魏朝不聽使者朝服，出何典禮？」

translations.literal: Zhaoming and the others said, "The Wei court will not allow envoys in court dress — what precedent does this come from?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoming and the others asked, "The Wei court will not allow envoys to wear court dress — what precedent is that based on?"

sentences.zh: 淹曰：「吉凶不相厭。

translations.literal: Yan said, "Auspicious and inauspicious do not mix.
translations.idiomatic: Yan replied, "Auspicious and inauspicious do not mix.

sentences.zh: 羔裘玄冠不以吊，此童稚所知也。

translations.literal: Lamb-skin robe and black cap are not worn for condolence visits — even children know this.
translations.idiomatic: A lamb-skin robe and black cap are not worn for condolence visits — even children know that.

sentences.zh: 昔季孫如晉，求遭喪之禮以行。

translations.literal: Long ago when Jisun went to Jin, he sought out the rites for encountering mourning before he traveled.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago, when Jisun went to Jin, he first asked what rites to follow upon encountering mourning.

sentences.zh: 今卿自江南遠來吊魏，方問出何典禮；

translations.literal: Now you have come from distant Jiangnan to offer condolences in Wei, and only now ask what precedent this comes from;
translations.idiomatic: You have come all the way from Jiangnan to offer condolences in Wei, and only now ask what precedent you should follow;

sentences.zh: 行人得失，何其遠哉！」

translations.literal: how far off are the envoy's gains and losses!"
translations.idiomatic: how far from proper conduct for an envoy you are!"

sentences.zh: 昭明曰：「二國之禮，應相準望。

translations.literal: Zhaoming said, "The rites of the two states ought to match each other.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoming said, "The rites of our two states ought to match each other.

sentences.zh: 齊高皇帝之喪，魏遣李彪來吊，初不素服，齊朝亦不以為疑，何至今日獨見要逼！」

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao of Qi died, Wei sent Li Biao to offer condolences; he wore no plain mourning garb at first, and the Qi court raised no objection — why must we alone be pressed today!"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao of Qi died, Wei sent Li Biao to offer condolences. He did not wear plain mourning dress at first, and the Qi court raised no objection. Why should we alone be forced today!"

sentences.zh: 淹曰：「齊不能行亮陰之禮，逾月即吉。

translations.literal: Yan said, "Qi could not observe the bright mourning rites and returned to normal dress after a month.
translations.idiomatic: Yan said, "Qi could not observe the full mourning rites and returned to normal dress after a month.

sentences.zh: 彪奉使之日，齊之君臣，鳴玉盈庭，貂璫曜目。

translations.literal: On the day Biao carried out his mission, Qi's lord and ministers filled the court with jade pendants chiming, sable-clad attendants dazzling the eye.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Biao carried out his mission, Qi's lord and ministers filled the court with chiming jade pendants and dazzling sable-clad attendants.

sentences.zh: 彪不得主人之命，敢獨以素服廁其間乎？

translations.literal: Without his host's command, how could Biao dare to appear among them alone in plain mourning dress?
translations.idiomatic: Without his host's command, how could Biao have dared to appear among them alone in plain mourning dress?

sentences.zh: 皇帝仁孝，侔於有虞，執親之喪，居廬食粥，豈得以此方彼乎？」

translations.literal: Our emperor is filial and humane, comparable to Yu of Shun; he keeps mourning for his parent, dwelling in a hut and eating coarse porridge — how can you compare that with the other case?"
translations.idiomatic: Our emperor is filial and humane, comparable to Shun of Yu; he keeps mourning for his parent, dwelling in a hut and eating coarse porridge. How can you compare the two cases?"

sentences.zh: 昭明曰：「三王不同禮，孰能知其得失！」

translations.literal: Zhaoming said, "The Three Sage Kings had different rites — who can know which was right or wrong!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoming said, "The Three Sage Kings had different rites — who can say which was right or wrong!"

sentences.zh: 淹曰：「然而虞舜、高宗皆非邪？」

translations.literal: Yan said, "And yet were Shun and Gaozong not correct?"
translations.idiomatic: Yan said, "And yet were Shun and Gaozong not correct?"

sentences.zh: 昭明、竣相顧而笑曰：「非孝者無親，何可當也！」

translations.literal: Zhaoming and Jun looked at each other and laughed, saying, "Those without filial piety have no parents — how can one argue with that!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoming and Jun looked at each other and laughed. "Those without filial piety have no parents," they said. "How can one argue with that!"

sentences.zh: 乃曰：「使人之來，唯繼褲褶，此既戌服，不可以吊，唯主人裁其吊服！

translations.literal: They then said, "We envoys came with only our embroidered trousers and jacket; as this is military dress, we cannot use it for condolences — only the host may decide our mourning attire!
translations.idiomatic: They then said, "We envoys brought only our embroidered trousers and jacket. As this is military dress, it cannot be worn for condolences — only the host may decide our mourning attire!

sentences.zh: 然違本朝之命，返必獲罪。」

translations.literal: Yet to defy our court's orders would bring punishment upon our return."
translations.idiomatic: But if we defy our own court's orders, we will be punished when we return."

sentences.zh: 淹曰：「使彼有君子，卿將命得宜，且有厚賞。

translations.literal: Yan said, "If your court has a gentleman in charge, you will have carried out your mission fittingly and will receive rich reward.
translations.idiomatic: Yan said, "If your court has a true gentleman in charge, you will have carried out your mission properly and will receive a rich reward.

sentences.zh: 若無君子，卿出而光國，得罪何妨！

translations.literal: If there is no gentleman, you will have gone forth and honored your state — what harm in incurring blame!
translations.idiomatic: If there is no such gentleman, you will have gone forth and honored your state — what harm is there in taking blame!

sentences.zh: 自當有良史書之。」

translations.literal: Surely worthy historians will record it."
translations.idiomatic: Surely worthy historians will record it."

sentences.zh: 乃以衣、□陷給昭明等，使服以致命。

translations.literal: He then gave Zhaoming and the others clothing and mourning caps and had them dress and deliver their message.
translations.idiomatic: He then gave Zhaoming and the others clothing and mourning caps and had them dress accordingly before delivering their message.

sentences.zh: 己丑，引昭明等入見，文武皆哭盡哀。

translations.literal: On jichou, Zhaoming and the others were led in to an audience; civil and military officials all wept their fill of grief.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jichou, Zhaoming and the others were led in to an audience, and civil and military officials all wept their fill of grief.

sentences.zh: 魏主嘉淹之敏，遷侍郎，賜絹百匹。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler praised Yan's quick wit, promoted him to Attendant, and granted him a hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei ruler praised Yan's quick wit, promoted him to attendant, and granted him a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 昭明，駰之子也。

translations.literal: Zhaoming was the son of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoming was the son of Yin.

sentences.zh: 始興簡王鑒卒。

translations.literal: Prince Jian of Shixing, Jian, died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian of Shixing, Jian, died.

sentences.zh: 三月，甲辰，魏主謁永固陵。

translations.literal: In the third month, on jiachen, the Wei ruler visited Yonggu Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day jiachen, the Wei ruler visited Yonggu Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，癸亥朔，設薦於太和廟。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, first day guihai, offerings were set at the Taihe Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the first day guihai, offerings were set out at the Taihe Temple.

sentences.zh: 魏主始進蔬食，追感哀哭，終日不飯；

translations.literal: The Wei ruler first took vegetarian food, was overcome with grief and wept, and went the whole day without eating;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei ruler first took vegetarian food, was overcome with grief and wept, and went the whole day without eating;

sentences.zh: 侍中馮誕等諫，經宿乃飯。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Feng Dan and others remonstrated; only after a full night did he eat.
translations.idiomatic: The palace attendant Feng Dan and others remonstrated with him, and only after a whole night had passed did he take food.

sentences.zh: 甲子，罷朝夕哭。

translations.literal: On jiazi, the morning-and-evening crying was discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiazi, the morning and evening mourning cries were discontinued.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，復謁永固陵。

translations.literal: On yichou, he again visited Yonggu Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yichou, he visited Yonggu Mausoleum again.

sentences.zh: 魏自正月不雨，至於癸酉，有司請祈百神，帝曰：「成湯遭旱，以至誠致雨，固不在曲禱山川。

translations.literal: Wei had had no rain since the first month; by guiyou, the responsible officials requested prayers to the hundred spirits. The Emperor said: "When King Cheng Tang encountered drought, he brought rain through utmost sincerity—it certainly lay not in bending prayers to mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei had gone without rain since the first month; by the day guiyou, the responsible officials asked to offer prayers to the hundred spirits. The emperor said, "When King Cheng Tang met with drought, he brought rain through utmost sincerity—it did not lie in twisting one's prayers toward mountains and rivers.

sentences.zh: 今普天喪恃，幽顯同哀，何宜四氣未周，遽行祀事！

translations.literal: Now all under Heaven mourns the loss of a pillar; the hidden and the manifest share the same grief—how can it be fitting, before the four seasons have run their course, hastily to carry out sacrificial rites!
translations.idiomatic: Now all under Heaven mourns the loss of its support; spirits and the living share the same grief. How can it be right, before the four seasons have fully turned, to rush ahead with sacrificial observances!

sentences.zh: 唯當責躬以待天遣。」

translations.literal: One should only reproach oneself and await Heaven's dispatch."
translations.idiomatic: One should only examine oneself and wait for what Heaven sends."

sentences.zh: 甲戌，魏員外散騎常侍李彪等來聘，為之置燕設樂。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Li Biao of Wei, supernumerary attendant cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, and others came on a friendly mission; for them a banquet was spread and music was provided.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiaxu, Li Biao of Northern Wei, supernumerary attendant cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, and others came on a friendly mission; the court prepared a banquet and arranged music for them.

sentences.zh: 彪辭樂，且曰：「主上孝思罔極，興墜正失。

translations.literal: Biao declined the music and said: "Our lord's filial thought knows no limit; he restores what has fallen and rectifies what has gone astray.
translations.idiomatic: Biao declined the music and said, "Our lord's filial devotion knows no bounds; he restores what has collapsed and sets right what has gone astray.

sentences.zh: 去三月晦，朝臣始除衰絰，猶以素服從事，是以使臣不敢承奏樂之賜。」

translations.literal: At the last day of the third month past, court ministers had only just removed their coarse hemp mourning; they still attend to affairs in plain mourning dress—therefore your envoy dares not accept the gift of musical performance."
translations.idiomatic: As of the last day of the third month, the court ministers had only just put aside their coarse hemp mourning bands and were still conducting affairs in plain mourning dress. For that reason your envoy dares not accept the gift of music."

sentences.zh: 朝廷從之。

translations.literal: The court assented.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 彪凡六奉使，上甚重之。

translations.literal: Biao had altogether six times served as envoy; the Emperor greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Biao had served as envoy six times in all; the emperor held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 將還，上親送至琅邪城，命群臣賦詩以寵之。

translations.literal: When he was about to return, the Emperor personally saw him off as far as Langye city and ordered the ministers to compose poems in his honor.
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to return, the emperor personally escorted him as far as Langye city and ordered the ministers to compose poems to honor him.

sentences.zh: 己卯，魏作明堂，改營太廟。

translations.literal: On jimao, Wei built the Bright Hall and reconstructed the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jimao, Northern Wei began building the Bright Hall and reconstructing the Grand Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 五月，己亥，魏主更定律令於東明觀，親決疑獄；

translations.literal: Fifth month, on jihai, the Wei ruler revised laws and ordinances at the Dongming Pavilion and personally decided doubtful cases;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the day jihai, the Wei ruler revised the laws and ordinances at the Dongming Pavilion and personally decided doubtful legal cases;

sentences.zh: 命李沖議定輕重，潤色辭旨，帝執筆書之。

translations.literal: he ordered Li Chong to determine severity and leniency and polish the wording; the Emperor took up the brush and wrote it out.
translations.idiomatic: he ordered Li Chong to determine penalties and polish the wording, while the emperor himself took up the brush and wrote out the text.

sentences.zh: 李沖忠勤明斷，加以慎密，為帝所委，情義無間；

translations.literal: Li Chong was loyal, diligent, clear, and decisive; moreover careful and discreet—entrusted by the Emperor, between them in feeling and duty there was no breach;
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong was loyal, diligent, clear-minded, and decisive, and besides that discreet and careful. The emperor entrusted him fully, and between them feeling and duty knew no breach;

sentences.zh: 舊臣貴戚，莫不心服，中外推之。

translations.literal: old ministers and honored kin—none failed to submit in heart; within and without the court all acclaimed him.
translations.idiomatic: old ministers and imperial kin alike submitted to him in heart, and he was acclaimed throughout the court and the realm.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，魏長孫百年攻洮陽、泥和二戍，克之，俘三千餘人。

translations.literal: On yimao, Wei's Changsun Bainian attacked the two garrisons of Taoyang and Nihe, took them, and captured more than three thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yimao, Changsun Bainian of Northern Wei attacked the garrisons at Taoyang and Nihe, captured them, and took more than three thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，魏初造五輅。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Wei for the first time made the five regalia chariots.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingchen, Northern Wei for the first time constructed the five ceremonial chariots.

sentences.zh: 六月，甲戌，以尚書左僕射王奐為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on jiaxu, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Huan was made governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the day jiaxu, Wang Huan, left vice director of the Masters of Writing, was appointed governor of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 丁未，魏濟陰王郁以貪殘賜死。

translations.literal: On dingwei, the Prince of Jiyin, Yu, was granted death for greed and cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingwei, Yu, Prince of Jiyin, was ordered to take his own life for greed and cruelty.

sentences.zh: 秋，閏七月，乙丑，魏主謁永固陵。

translations.literal: Autumn, intercalary seventh month, on yichou, the Wei ruler visited Yonggu Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the intercalary seventh month, on the day yichou, the Wei ruler visited Yonggu Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 己卯，魏主詔曰：「烈祖有創業之功。

translations.literal: On jimao, the Wei ruler issued an edict saying: "The Illustrious Ancestor had the achievement of founding the enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jimao, the Wei ruler issued an edict stating, "The Illustrious Ancestor had the achievement of founding the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 世祖有開拓之德，宜為祖宗，百世不遷。

translations.literal: The Shizu had the virtue of opening and expanding—he should serve as a founding ancestor, unmoved for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: The Shizu possessed the virtue of expansion and conquest and should stand as a founding ancestor, never to be displaced for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 平文之功少於昭成，而廟號太祖，道武之功高於平文，而廟號烈祖，於義未允。

translations.literal: Pingwen's achievements were less than Zhaocheng's, yet his temple title was Grand Ancestor; Daowu's achievements were greater than Pingwen's, yet his temple title was Illustrious Ancestor—in principle this was not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Pingwen's achievements were lesser than those of Emperor Zhaocheng, yet he bore the temple title Grand Ancestor; Emperor Daowu's achievements surpassed those of Emperor Pingwen, yet he bore the temple title Illustrious Ancestor. By right this was not fitting.

sentences.zh: 朕今奉尊烈祖為太祖，以世祖、顯祖為二祧，餘皆以次而遷。」

translations.literal: We now exalt the Illustrious Ancestor as Grand Ancestor, take the Shizu and Xianzu as the two branch shrines, and move the rest down in order."
translations.idiomatic: We now honor the Illustrious Ancestor as Grand Ancestor, establish the Shizu and Xianzu as the two branch ancestral shrines, and shift the rest down in order."

sentences.zh: 八月，壬辰，又詔議養老及禋於六宗之禮。

translations.literal: Eighth month, on renchen, another edict ordered discussion of the rites for nurturing the aged and the yin sacrifice to the Six Ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the day renchen, another edict ordered discussion of the rites for honoring the aged and for the yin sacrifice to the Six Ancestors.

sentences.zh: 先是，魏常以正月吉日於朝廷設幕，中置松柏樹，設五帝座而祠之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wei had often on an auspicious day of the first month set up a canopy at court, placed pine and cypress trees within it, set out seats for the Five Emperors, and sacrificed to them.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, Northern Wei had often set up a canopy at court on an auspicious day in the first month, placed pine and cypress trees within it, arranged seats for the Five Emperors, and sacrificed to them.

sentences.zh: 又有探策之祭。

translations.literal: There was also the rite of divination by lots.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a rite of divination by drawing lots.

sentences.zh: 帝皆以為非禮，罷之。

translations.literal: The Emperor regarded them all as contrary to ritual and abolished them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor considered all of these contrary to proper rite and abolished them.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，移道壇於桑干之陰，改曰崇虛寺。

translations.literal: On wuxu, the Dao altar was moved to the north bank of the Sanggan and renamed Chongxu Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuxu, the Dao altar was moved to the north bank of the Sanggan River and renamed Chongxu Temple.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，帝引見群臣，問以「『禘祫』，王、鄭之義，是非安在？」

translations.literal: On yisi, the Emperor summoned the ministers and asked them, "Regarding 'di and xia,' where does right and wrong lie in the interpretations of Wang and Zheng?"
translations.idiomatic: On the day yisi, the emperor received the ministers and asked them, "Regarding di and xia, where does right and wrong lie in the interpretations of Wang and Zheng?"

sentences.zh: 尚書游明根等從鄭，中書監高閭等從王。

translations.literal: Minister of Writing You Minggen and others followed Zheng; Director of the Palace Secretariat Gao Lu and others followed Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Writing You Minggen and others followed Zheng's view; Director of the Palace Secretariat Gao Lu and others followed Wang's view.

sentences.zh: 詔：「圜丘、宗廟皆有禘名，從鄭：禘祫並為一祭，從王：著之於令。」

translations.literal: Edict: "Both the Circular Mound and the Ancestral Temple bear the name di—following Zheng: di and xia are one sacrifice; following Wang: record this in the ordinance."
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated, "Both the Circular Mound and the Ancestral Temple bear the name di—following Zheng's view, di and xia are one sacrifice; following Wang's view, this is to be recorded in the ordinance."

sentences.zh: 戊午，又詔：「國家饗祀諸神，凡一千二百餘處；

translations.literal: On wuwu, another edict: "The state feeds and sacrifices to the spirits at more than twelve hundred places;
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuwu, another edict stated, "The state performs feasts and sacrifices to the spirits at more than twelve hundred sites;

sentences.zh: 今欲減省群祀，務從簡約。」

translations.literal: we now wish to reduce and cut back the multitude of sacrifices, striving for simplicity."
translations.idiomatic: we now wish to cut back the multitude of sacrifices and keep them as simple as possible."

sentences.zh: 又詔：「明堂、太廟，配祭、配享，於斯備矣。

translations.literal: Another edict: "At the Bright Hall and Grand Temple, associated offerings and associated sharing are now complete.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict stated, "At the Bright Hall and Grand Ancestral Temple, associated offerings and shared worship are now fully provided for.

sentences.zh: 白登、崞山、雞鳴山廟，唯遣有司行事。

translations.literal: The temples at Baideng, Guoshan, and Jiming Mountain—only send the responsible officials to perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: As for the temples at Baideng, Guoshan, and Jiming Mountain, only send the responsible officials to perform the rites.

sentences.zh: 馮宣王廟在長安，宜敕雍州以時供祭。」

translations.literal: The Temple of Prince Xuan of Feng is at Chang'an—Yong Province should be ordered to supply sacrifices at the proper times."
translations.idiomatic: The temple of Prince Xuan of the Feng clan stands at Chang'an; Yong Province should be instructed to provide sacrifices at the proper seasons."

sentences.zh: 又詔：「先有水火之神四十餘名及城北星神，今圜丘之下既祭風伯、雨師、司中、司命，明堂祭門、戶、井、灶、中霤，四十神悉可罷之。」

translations.literal: Another edict: "Formerly there were more than forty spirits of water and fire and the star spirit north of the city; now beneath the Circular Mound are sacrificed the Earl of Wind, the Master of Rain, the Director of the Center, and the Director of Fate; at the Bright Hall are sacrificed the gate, the doorway, the well, the stove, and the central drain—all forty spirits may be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict stated, "Formerly there were more than forty water-and-fire spirits and the star spirit north of the city wall. Now that the Circular Mound sacrifices to the Earl of Wind, the Master of Rain, the Director of the Center, and the Director of Fate, and the Bright Hall sacrifices to the gate, doorway, well, stove, and central drain, all forty of those spirits may be abolished."

sentences.zh: 甲寅，詔曰：「近論朝日、夕月，皆欲以二分之日於東、西郊行禮。

translations.literal: On jiayin, an edict said: "In recent discussion of the morning sun and evening moon rites, all wished to perform them on the days of the two equinoxes at the eastern and western suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiayin, an edict stated, "In recent discussion of the morning sun and evening moon rites, all agreed they should be performed on the days of the two equinoxes at the eastern and western suburbs.

sentences.zh: 然月有餘閏，行無常准。

translations.literal: Yet the moon has surplus and intercalation; practice has no fixed standard.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the moon has extra days and intercalary months, so there is no fixed standard for carrying this out.

sentences.zh: 若一依分日，或值月於東而行禮於西，序情即理，不可施行。

translations.literal: If one strictly followed the equinox days, sometimes the moon would be in the east while the rite was performed in the west—in sentiment and principle this could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: If one strictly followed the equinox days, the moon might still be in the east while the rite was performed in the west. In feeling as in reason, this could not be carried out.

sentences.zh: 昔秘書監薛謂等以為朝日以朔，夕月以朏。

translations.literal: In the past Director of the Secretariat Xue Wei and others held that the morning sun rite should be on the new moon and the evening moon rite on the third-day moon.
translations.idiomatic: In the past Xue Wei, director of the Secretariat, and others held that the morning sun rite should fall on the day of the new moon and the evening moon rite on the day of the third-day moon.

sentences.zh: 卿等意謂朔朏、二分，何者為是？」

translations.literal: In your view, new moon and third-day moon, or the two equinoxes—which is correct?"
translations.idiomatic: In your view, should the rites follow the new and third-day moons, or the two equinoxes? Which is correct?"

sentences.zh: 尚書游明根等請用朔朏，從之。

translations.literal: Minister of Writing You Minggen and others requested using the new and third-day moons—the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Writing You Minggen and others asked to follow the new and third-day moons, and this was approved.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，魏有司上言，求卜祥日。

translations.literal: On bingchen, the Wei responsible officials submitted a memorial requesting divination for an auspicious day.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingchen, the responsible officials of Northern Wei submitted a memorial asking to divine an auspicious day.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「筮日求吉，既乖敬事之志，又違永慕之心；

translations.literal: Edict: "Divining a day to seek good fortune both departs from the intent of reverent service and violates the heart of everlasting longing;
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated, "To divine a day in search of good fortune both departs from the spirit of reverent service and violates the heart of everlasting longing;

sentences.zh: 今直用晦日。」

translations.literal: now simply use the last day of the month."
translations.idiomatic: use the last day of the month directly."

sentences.zh: 九月，丁丑夜，帝宿於廟，帥群臣哭已，帝易服縞冠、革帶、黑屨，侍臣易服黑介幘、白絹單衣、革帶、烏履，遂哭盡乙夜。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on the night of dingchou, the Emperor lodged at the temple; after leading the ministers in weeping, the Emperor changed into a white mourning cap, leather belt, and black shoes; attendants changed into black mourning caps, white silk unlined garments, leather belts, and black shoes; they wept until the second watch of the night.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the night of dingchou, the emperor lodged at the temple. After leading the ministers in mourning, the emperor changed into a white mourning cap, leather belt, and black shoes; the attending ministers changed into black mourning caps, white silk unlined garments, leather belts, and black shoes; and they continued weeping until the second watch of the night.

sentences.zh: 戊子晦，帝易祭服，縞冠素紕、白布深衣、麻繩履，侍臣去幘易□陷。

translations.literal: On wuzi, the last day of the month, the Emperor changed into sacrificial dress—white mourning cap with plain hem, white cloth deep garment, hemp-cord shoes; attendants removed their caps and changed into mourning cloths.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, the last day of the month, the emperor changed into sacrificial dress—a white mourning cap with plain hem, a white cloth deep garment, and hemp-cord shoes; the attending ministers removed their caps and changed into mourning cloths.

sentences.zh: 既祭，出廟，帝立哭。

translations.literal: After the sacrifice, leaving the temple, the Emperor stood and wept.
translations.idiomatic: After the sacrifice, as he left the temple, the emperor stood and wept.

sentences.zh: 久之，乃還。

translations.literal: After a long while, he then returned.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while, he returned.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，魏明堂、太廟成。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, Wei's Bright Hall and Grand Temple were completed.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Northern Wei's Bright Hall and Grand Ancestral Temple were completed.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，魏主謁永固陵，毀瘠猶甚。

translations.literal: On gengyin, the Wei ruler visited Yonggu Mausoleum; his emaciation from mourning was still severe.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengyin, the Wei ruler visited Yonggu Mausoleum; he was still severely emaciated from mourning.

sentences.zh: 司空穆亮諫曰：「陛下祥練已闋，號慕如始。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Mu Liang remonstrated, saying: "Your Majesty's period of unlucky and lucky mourning garments has already ended, yet your crying and longing are as at the beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Mu Liang remonstrated, saying, "Your Majesty's mourning period has already ended, yet your wailing and longing are as intense as at the beginning.

sentences.zh: 王者為天地所子，為萬民父母，未有子過哀而父母不戚，父母憂而子獨悅豫者也。

translations.literal: The king is the son of Heaven and Earth and the father and mother of the myriad people—never has a child grieved excessively while the parents did not sorrow, or the parents worried while the child alone rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: The king is the son of Heaven and Earth and father and mother to the myriad people. Never has a child grieved excessively while the parents did not sorrow, or the parents been troubled while the child alone took comfort.

sentences.zh: 今和氣不應，風旱為災，願陛下襲輕服，御常膳，鑾輿時動，鹹秩百神，庶使天人交慶。」

translations.literal: Now the harmonious qi does not respond; wind and drought become disasters. We hope Your Majesty will assume light mourning dress, take ordinary meals, move the imperial carriage from time to time, and order sacrifices to the hundred spirits—perhaps Heaven and men may together rejoice."
translations.idiomatic: Now the harmonious qi does not respond, and wind and drought bring disaster. We ask that Your Majesty put on lighter mourning dress, take ordinary meals, move the imperial carriage from time to time, and order sacrifices to the hundred spirits, so that Heaven and mankind may together rejoice."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「孝悌之至，無所不通。

translations.literal: Edict: "Filial and fraternal devotion at its utmost passes through everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied, "Filial and fraternal devotion at its utmost reaches everywhere.

sentences.zh: 今飄風、旱氣，皆誠慕未濃，幽顯無感也。

translations.literal: Now the whirling wind and drought qi—all are because sincere longing is not yet deep; hidden and manifest have not been moved.
translations.idiomatic: The whirling winds and drought now are all because sincere longing is not yet deep enough; neither spirits nor the living have been moved.

sentences.zh: 所言過哀之咎，諒為未衷。」

translations.literal: What you say about the fault of excessive grief—I am sure is not the inner truth."
translations.idiomatic: What you say about the fault of excessive grief—I am sure does not hit the mark."

sentences.zh: 十一月，己未朔，魏主禫於太和廟，兗冕以祭。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, first day of jiwei, the Wei ruler performed the final mourning sacrifice at the Taihe Temple, wearing the ceremonial cap and robes of investiture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the first day jiwei, the Wei ruler performed the final mourning sacrifice at the Taihe Temple, wearing full ceremonial cap and robes.

sentences.zh: 既而服黑介幘，素紗深衣，拜陵而還。

translations.literal: Afterward he wore a black mourning cap and plain silk deep garment, paid respects at the mausoleum, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he wore a black mourning cap and plain silk deep garment, paid his respects at the mausoleum, and returned.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，冬至，魏主祀圜丘，遂祀明堂，還，至太和廟，乃入。

translations.literal: On guihai, the winter solstice, the Wei ruler sacrificed at the Circular Mound, then sacrificed at the Bright Hall; returning, he reached the Taihe Temple, and only then entered.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, the day of the winter solstice, the Wei ruler sacrificed at the Circular Mound, then at the Bright Hall; on returning he reached the Taihe Temple before going inside.

sentences.zh: 甲子，臨太華殿，服通天冠，絳紗袍，以饗群臣。

translations.literal: On jiazi, he attended the Taihua Hall, wore the universal-penetration cap and crimson silk robe, and feasted the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiazi, he attended court at the Taihua Hall, wearing the universal-penetration cap and crimson silk robe, and gave a feast for the ministers.

sentences.zh: 樂縣而不作。

translations.literal: Musical bells were suspended but not played.
translations.idiomatic: Musical bells were set in place but not played.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，服兗冕，辭太和廟，帥百官奉神主遷於新廟。

translations.literal: On dingmao, wearing investiture cap and robes, he took leave at the Taihe Temple, led the hundred officials in escorting the spirit tablets, and moved them to the new temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingmao, wearing full ceremonial cap and robes, he took leave at the Taihe Temple, led the hundred officials in escorting the spirit tablets, and moved them to the new temple.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，魏大定官品。

translations.literal: On yihai, Wei greatly fixed official ranks.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yihai, Northern Wei established its official ranks in full.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，考諸牧守。

translations.literal: On wuxu, the various regional governors were examined.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuxu, the various provincial and commandery governors were evaluated.

sentences.zh: 魏假通直散騎常侍李彪等來聘。

translations.literal: Wei's acting direct attendant cavalier attendant-in-ordinary Li Biao and others came on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: Li Biao of Northern Wei, acting direct attendant cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, and others came on a friendly mission.

sentences.zh: 魏舊制，群臣季冬朝賀，服褲褶行事，謂之小歲；

translations.literal: Wei's old regulation: at the end-of-year court congratulations in late winter, ministers wore trousers and jackets in attending to affairs—this was called the minor year;
translations.idiomatic: By Northern Wei's old regulation, at the end-of-year court congratulations in late winter, the ministers wore trousers and split jackets when attending to affairs—this was called the minor year;

sentences.zh: 丙戌，詔罷之。

translations.literal: On bingxu, an edict abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingxu, an edict abolished the practice.

sentences.zh: 十二月，壬辰，魏遷社於內城之西。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on renchen, Wei moved the Earth altar to the west inside the inner city.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day renchen, Northern Wei moved the altar of the soil to the west side of the inner city.

sentences.zh: 魏以安定王休為太傅，劉郡王簡為太保。

translations.literal: Wei made Prince of Anding, Xiu, Grand Tutor, and Prince of Liu Commandery, Jian, Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei appointed Prince Xiu of Anding as Grand Tutor and Prince Jian of Qi Commandery as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 高麗王璉卒，壽百餘歲。

translations.literal: The King of Goguryeo, Ryeon, died; he was more than a hundred years old.
translations.idiomatic: Ryeon, king of Goguryeo, died at more than a hundred years of age.

sentences.zh: 魏主為之制素委貌，布深衣，舉哀於東郊；

translations.literal: The Wei ruler for him arranged plain Weimao caps and cloth deep garments and mourned at the eastern suburb;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei ruler had plain Weimao caps and cloth deep garments made for the occasion and led mourning rites at the eastern suburb;

sentences.zh: 遣謁者僕射李安上策贈太傅，謚曰康。

translations.literal: he sent Chief of Court Intendants Li An to present an appointment edict posthumously granting the title Grand Tutor, with posthumous name Kang.
translations.idiomatic: he sent Li An, chief of court intendant-attendants, to present an edict posthumously granting him the title Grand Tutor and the posthumous name Kang.

sentences.zh: 孫雲嗣立。

translations.literal: His grandson Yun succeeded and was established.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Yun succeeded to the throne.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，魏主始迎春於東郊。

translations.literal: On yiyou, the Wei ruler for the first time welcomed spring at the eastern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yiyou, the Wei ruler for the first time welcomed spring at the eastern suburb.

sentences.zh: 自是四時迎氣皆親之。

translations.literal: From this onward, welcoming the qi of the four seasons—he personally attended to all of them.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he personally attended every seasonal welcoming of the qi.

sentences.zh: 初，魏世祖克統萬及姑臧，獲雅樂器服工人，並存之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wei Shizu conquered Tongwan and Guzang, he obtained elegant music instruments, garments, and craftsmen, and preserved them all.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Shizu of Northern Wei conquered Tongwan and Guzang, he captured elegant musical instruments, vestments, and craftsmen, and preserved them all.

sentences.zh: 其後累朝無留意者，樂工浸盡，音制多亡。

translations.literal: Afterward, successive courts paid them no attention; musicians gradually perished, and many musical systems were lost.
translations.idiomatic: Later courts paid them no attention; musicians gradually died off, and much of the musical tradition was lost.

sentences.zh: 高祖始命有司訪民間曉音律者，議定雅樂，當時無能知者。

translations.literal: Gaozu first ordered the responsible officials to seek among the people those who understood pitch and rhythm, to discuss and fix elegant music—but at the time none could be found who knew it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu first ordered the responsible officials to seek out people in the realm who understood pitch and rhythm to discuss and establish elegant music, but at the time no one could be found who knew it.

sentences.zh: 然金、石、羽旄之飾，稍壯麗於往時矣。

translations.literal: Yet the adornments of metal, stone, feathers, and banners were somewhat more splendid than in former times.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, the adornments of bells, stones, feathers, and banners were somewhat more splendid than in former times.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，詔簡置樂官，使修其職，又命中書監高閭參定。

translations.literal: On xinhai, an edict ordered selection and establishment of music officials to perform their duties; the Director of the Palace Secretariat Gao Lu was also ordered to join in fixing it.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinhai, an edict ordered the selection and appointment of music officials to restore their duties, and also directed Gao Lu, director of the Palace Secretariat, to join in fixing the standards.

sentences.zh: 初，晉張斐、杜預共注《律》三十卷，自泰始以來用之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jin's Zhang Fei and Du Yu jointly annotated the Penal Code in thirty juan; since Taishi it had been used.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhang Fei and Du Yu of Jin jointly annotated the Penal Code in thirty chapters, and it had been used since the Taishi era.

sentences.zh: 《律》文簡約，或一章之中，兩家所處，生殺頓異，臨時斟酌，吏得為奸。

translations.literal: The text of the Code was terse; within a single chapter, the two schools' treatments could differ sharply on life and death; temporary weighing gave clerks room for fraud.
translations.idiomatic: The text of the Code was terse; within a single chapter the two schools' rulings on life and death could differ sharply, and when officials weighed matters on the spot, clerks found room for fraud.

sentences.zh: 上留心法令，詔獄官詳正舊注。

translations.literal: The Emperor attended to laws and ordinances and ordered prison officials to examine and correct the old annotations in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned his attention to the laws and ordered prison officials to examine and correct the old annotations in detail.

sentences.zh: 七年，尚書刪定郎王植集定二注，表奏之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Review-and-Fixation Officer of the Masters of Writing Wang Zhi compiled and fixed the two annotations and submitted them in memorial.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, Wang Zhi, review-and-fixation officer of the Masters of Writing, compiled and reconciled the two annotations and submitted them in memorial.

sentences.zh: 詔公卿、八座參議考正，竟陵王子良總其事；

translations.literal: An edict ordered the dukes and ministers and the Eight Seats to join in discussion, examination, and correction; Prince of Jingling, Ziliang, oversaw the affair;
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the dukes, ministers, and Eight Seats to join in discussion and correction; Prince Ziliang of Jingling oversaw the work;

sentences.zh: 眾議異同不能壹者，制旨平決。

translations.literal: where the assembled discussions differed and could not be unified, the imperial decision settled them.
translations.idiomatic: where the assembled discussions could not be reconciled, the imperial decision settled the matter.

sentences.zh: 是歲，書成。

translations.literal: That year, the book was completed.
translations.idiomatic: That year the work was completed.

sentences.zh: 廷尉山陰孔稚珪上表，以為：「《律》文雖定，苟用失其平，則法書徒明於帙裡，冤魂猶結於獄中。

translations.literal: Commandant of Justice Kong Zhigui of Shanyin submitted a memorial, holding: "Although the text of the Code is fixed, if application loses its balance, then the law book will merely shine in its pages while wronged souls still bind themselves in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Zhigui of Shanyin, commandant of justice, submitted a memorial arguing that "although the text of the Code was now fixed, if application lost its balance the law book would merely shine between its covers while wronged souls still lingered in prison.

sentences.zh: 竊尋古之名流，多有法學；

translations.literal: I privately reflect that ancient eminent men mostly had legal learning;
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that eminent men of old mostly possessed legal learning;

sentences.zh: 今之士子，莫肯為業。

translations.literal: today's scholar-gentlemen are unwilling to make it their profession.
translations.idiomatic: today's scholar-gentlemen are unwilling to make it their profession.

sentences.zh: 縱有習者，世議所輕，將恐此書永淪走吏之手矣。

translations.literal: even if there are those who study it, public opinion holds them in low regard—I fear this book will forever fall into the hands of running clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Even when there are those who study it, public opinion holds them in contempt, and I fear this book will forever fall into the hands of low-level clerks.

sentences.zh: 今若置《律》助教，依《五經》例，國子生有欲讀者，策試高第，即加擢用，以補內外之官，庶幾士流有所勸慕。」

translations.literal: If now a Penal Code assistant instructor were established, following the Five Classics precedent—Imperial University students who wish to read it, if they rank high on written examination, would immediately be promoted and selected to fill posts within and without the court—perhaps the scholar class would have something to encourage and admire."
translations.idiomatic: If a Penal Code assistant instructor were now established on the model of the Five Classics, Imperial University students who wished to study it could, if they ranked high on examination, be promoted at once to fill posts within and without the court, and perhaps the scholar class would have something to aspire to."

sentences.zh: 詔從其請，事竟不行。

translations.literal: The edict granted his request, but in the end the matter was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved his request, but in the end the proposal was never implemented.

sentences.zh: 初，林邑王范陽邁，世相承襲，夷人范當根純攻奪其國，遣使獻金簟等物。

translations.literal: Earlier, the King of Linyi, Fan Yang Mai, had been passed down through generations; the barbarian Fan Danggen Chun seized his state by attack, sent envoys presenting golden mats and other goods.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Fan Yang Mai, king of Linyi, had ruled through successive generations until the barbarian Fan Danggen Chun seized the kingdom by force and sent envoys presenting golden mats and other goods.

sentences.zh: 詔以當根純為都督緣海諸軍事、林邑王。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Danggen Chun as commander of all military affairs along the coast and King of Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Danggen Chun commander of all military affairs along the coast and king of Linyi.

sentences.zh: 魏冀州刺史咸陽王禧入朝。

translations.literal: Yuan Xi, Prince of Xianyang, governor of Jizhou in Wei, came to court.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xi, Prince of Xianyang and governor of Jizhou, came to court at Wei.

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「冀州民三千人稱禧清明有惠政，請世胙冀州。」

translations.literal: The responsible officials memorialized: "Three thousand people of Jizhou praise Xi's clear-mindedness and benevolent governance, and request that he receive hereditary sacrificial fief in Jizhou."
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials memorialized, "Three thousand people of Jizhou praised Xi's clear-minded and benevolent rule and asked that he be granted hereditary sacrificial rights in Jizhou."

sentences.zh: 魏主詔曰：「利建雖古，未必今宜；

translations.literal: The Wei ruler said: "Establishing feudal domains is an ancient practice, but it is not necessarily suitable today;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei ruler replied, "Establishing feudal domains is an ancient practice, but it is not necessarily suited to the present age;

sentences.zh: 經野由君，理非下情。」

translations.literal: governing the wilds is the ruler's prerogative; it is not a matter for popular sentiment to decide."
translations.idiomatic: governing the realm is the ruler's prerogative, not something to be decided by popular petition."

sentences.zh: 以禧為司州牧、都督司、豫等六州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Xi was made governor of Sizhou and commander of all military affairs in six provinces including Si and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was instead appointed governor of Sizhou and commander of all military affairs in six provinces, including Si and Yu.

sentences.zh: 初，魏文明太后寵任宦者略陽苻承祖，官至侍中，知都曹事，賜以不死之詔。

translations.literal: Earlier, Empress Dowager Wenming of Wei favored and entrusted the eunuch Fu Chengzu of Lueyang; he reached the office of attendant-in-ordinary, managed the affairs of the Capital Bureau, and was granted an edict of immunity from death.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Empress Dowager Wenming of Northern Wei had favored the eunuch Fu Chengzu of Lueyang, elevating him to attendant-in-ordinary and putting him in charge of the Capital Bureau; he was even granted an edict guaranteeing he would not be put to death.

sentences.zh: 太后殂，承祖坐贓應死，魏主原之，削職禁錮於家，仍除悖義將軍，封佞濁子，月餘而卒。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager died, Chengzu was convicted of corruption and deserved death; the Wei ruler pardoned him, stripped his office, and confined him at home, yet still appointed him General of Perverse Righteousness and enfeoffed him as Marquis Vile-Sycophant; after a little more than a month he died.
translations.idiomatic: After the empress dowager died, Chengzu was found guilty of corruption and sentenced to death. The Wei ruler pardoned him, stripped him of office, and confined him at home, yet still appointed him General of Perverse Righteousness and enfeoffed him as Marquis Vile-Sycophant. A little over a month later he died.

sentences.zh: 承祖方用事，親姻爭趨附以求利。

translations.literal: While Chengzu was in power, relatives by marriage all rushed to attach themselves to him seeking profit.
translations.idiomatic: While Chengzu held power, his relatives by marriage all rushed to attach themselves to him in hope of gain.

sentences.zh: 其從母楊氏為姚氏婦獨否，常謂承祖之母曰：「姊雖有一時之榮，不若妹有無憂之樂。」

translations.literal: His maternal aunt, née Yang, who had married into the Yao clan, alone refused; she often told Chengzu's mother, "Elder sister, though you have glory for a time, it is not equal to younger sister's carefree joy."
translations.idiomatic: His maternal aunt, née Yang, who had married into the Yao clan, alone refused to join them. She often told Chengzu's mother, "Sister, your momentary glory is nothing compared with the peace I enjoy without worry."

sentences.zh: 姊與之衣服，多不受；

translations.literal: When her elder sister gave her clothes, she mostly would not accept them;
translations.idiomatic: When her sister gave her clothes, she usually refused them;

sentences.zh: 強與之，則曰：「我夫家世貧，美衣服使人不安。」

translations.literal: if forced to take them, she would say, "My husband's family has been poor for generations; fine clothes make one ill at ease."
translations.idiomatic: and if pressed to accept them, she would say, "My husband's family has been poor for generations. Fine clothes only make me uncomfortable."

sentences.zh: 不得已，或受而埋之。

translations.literal: When she had no choice, she sometimes accepted them and buried them.
translations.idiomatic: When she had no choice, she sometimes accepted them and buried them.

sentences.zh: 與之奴婢，則曰：「我家無食，不能飼也。」

translations.literal: When given slave-girls and servants, she would say, "My household has no food and cannot feed them."
translations.idiomatic: When given slaves and maidservants, she would say, "My household has no food and cannot keep them."

sentences.zh: 常著弊衣，自執勞苦。

translations.literal: She always wore worn clothes and performed hard labor herself.
translations.idiomatic: She always wore patched clothes and did hard labor herself.

sentences.zh: 承祖遣車迎之，不肯起；

translations.literal: Chengzu sent a carriage to fetch her, but she would not rise;
translations.idiomatic: Chengzu sent a carriage to fetch her, but she refused to get up;

sentences.zh: 強使人抱置車上，則大哭曰：「爾欲殺我！」

translations.literal: when men forcibly lifted her and placed her in the carriage, she wept loudly and said, "You mean to kill me!"
translations.idiomatic: when men forcibly lifted her into the carriage, she burst into tears and cried, "You mean to kill me!"

sentences.zh: 由是苻氏內外號為「癡姨」。

translations.literal: From this, inside and outside the Fu clan she was called "Mad Aunt."
translations.idiomatic: From then on, everyone in the Fu clan, inside and out, called her "Mad Aunt."

sentences.zh: 及承祖敗，有司執其二姨至殿廷。

translations.literal: When Chengzu fell, the responsible officials seized his two maternal aunts and brought them to the palace hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzu fell from power, the responsible officials seized his two maternal aunts and brought them before the throne.

sentences.zh: 其一姨伏法。

translations.literal: One aunt was executed according to law.
translations.idiomatic: One aunt was executed.

sentences.zh: 帝見姚氏姨貧弊，特赦之。

translations.literal: The emperor saw that the Yao-clan aunt was poor and wretched, and specially pardoned her.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that the aunt who had married into the Yao clan lived in poverty, the emperor specially pardoned her.

sentences.zh: 李惠之誅也，思皇后之昆弟皆死。

translations.literal: When Li Hui was executed, the brothers of Empress Si all died.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Hui was executed, all the brothers of Empress Si were put to death.

sentences.zh: 惠從弟鳳為安樂王長樂主簿，長樂坐不軌，誅，鳳亦坐死。

translations.literal: Hui's younger cousin Feng served as chief clerk to Chang Le, Prince of Anle; Chang Le was convicted of treason and executed, and Feng also died by association.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's younger cousin Feng had served as chief clerk to Chang Le, Prince of Anle. When Chang Le was convicted of treason and executed, Feng was put to death as well.

sentences.zh: 鳳子安祖等四人逃匿獲免，遇赦乃出。

translations.literal: Feng's sons Anzu and three others escaped and hid, thereby surviving; they emerged only after an amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Feng's sons Anzu and three others escaped and hid, surviving only because an amnesty was later declared.

sentences.zh: 既而魏主訪舅氏存者，得安祖等，皆封候，加將軍。

translations.literal: Later the Wei ruler inquired after surviving maternal relatives and found Anzu and the others; all were enfeoffed as marquises and given generalships.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Wei ruler inquired after surviving maternal relatives and found Anzu and the others. All were enfeoffed as marquises and given generalships.

sentences.zh: 既而引見，謂曰：「卿之先世，再獲罪於時。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he received them in audience and said, "Your forebears twice incurred guilt in their time.
translations.idiomatic: He soon received them in audience and said, "Your forebears twice fell afoul of the times.

sentences.zh: 王者設官以待賢才，由外戚而舉者，季世之法也。

translations.literal: A king establishes offices to await men of talent; raising men through maternal kin is the practice of a decadent age.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler establishes offices to await men of talent. Promoting men simply because they are maternal kin is the practice of a decadent age.

sentences.zh: 卿等既無異能，且可還家。

translations.literal: Since you have no special ability, for now you may return home.
translations.idiomatic: Since you possess no special ability, you may as well return home for now.

sentences.zh: 自今外戚無能者視此。」

translations.literal: From now on, maternal kin without ability should look to this as the model."
translations.idiomatic: From now on, maternal kin without ability should take this as their model."

sentences.zh: 後又例降爵為伯，去其軍號。

translations.literal: Later, by precedent their ranks were reduced to earl and their military titles removed.
translations.idiomatic: Later, by precedent, their ranks were reduced to earl and their military titles were removed.

sentences.zh: 時人皆以為帝待馮氏太厚，待顧氏太薄；

translations.literal: People of the time all thought the emperor treated the Feng clan too generously and the Gu clan too stingily;
translations.idiomatic: People at the time all thought the emperor treated the Feng clan too generously and the Gu clan too stingily;

sentences.zh: 太常高閭嘗以為言，帝不聽。

translations.literal: Minister of Ceremonies Gao Lu once spoke of this, but the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Ceremonies Gao Lu once raised the point, but the emperor would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 及世宗尊寵外家，乃以安祖弟興祖為中山太守，追贈李惠開府儀同三司、中山公，謚曰莊。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong honored and favored his maternal kin, he made Anzu's younger brother Xingzu governor of Zhongshan, posthumously enfeoffed Li Hui as grand marshal with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies and Duke of Zhongshan, and gave him the posthumous title Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong came to honor his maternal kin, he appointed Anzu's younger brother Xingzu governor of Zhongshan, posthumously enfeoffed Li Hui as grand marshal with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies and Duke of Zhongshan, and gave him the posthumous title Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 世祖武皇帝中永明十年（

translations.literal: Tenth year of Yongming, middle period of Emperor Wu the Founding Ancestor (
translations.idiomatic: Tenth year of Yongming of Emperor Wu of Qi (

sentences.zh: 壬申，公元四九二年）

translations.literal: renshen, the year 492 CE)
translations.idiomatic: renshen, A.D. 492)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，戊午朔，魏主朝饗群臣於太華殿，懸而不樂。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the first day wuwu, the Wei ruler held morning feast for the ministers in Taihua Hall; bells were hung but no music was played.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the new moon of wuwu, the Wei ruler held a morning feast for his ministers in Taihua Hall, with bells hung but no music played.

sentences.zh: 己未，魏主宗祀顯祖於明堂以配上帝，遂登靈台以觀雲物，降居青陽左個，布政事。

translations.literal: On jiwei, the Wei ruler performed ancestral sacrifice to the Illustrious Ancestor in the Bright Hall to match the Supreme Lord, then ascended the Spirit Terrace to observe cloud signs, descended to dwell in the left chamber of Qingyang, and issued government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiwei, the Wei ruler sacrificed to the Illustrious Ancestor in the Bright Hall to accompany the Supreme Lord, then ascended the Spirit Terrace to observe celestial signs, descended to the left chamber of Qingyang, and there conducted state business.

sentences.zh: 自是每朔依以為常。

translations.literal: From this, on every new moon he followed this as the regular practice.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he made this his regular practice at every new moon.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍庾蓽等聘於魏，魏主使侍郎成淹引蓽等於館南，瞻望行禮。

translations.literal: Attendant cavalier attendant-in-ordinary Yu Bi and others went on a mission of courtesy to Wei; the Wei ruler sent Gentleman Cheng Yan to lead Bi and the others south of the guest house to gaze from afar and perform rites.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bi, attendant cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, and others went on a diplomatic mission to Wei. The Wei ruler sent Gentleman Cheng Yan to lead them south of the guest house to gaze from afar and perform the rites of respect.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，魏始以太祖配南郊。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Wei for the first time paired the Grand Ancestor at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinyou, Wei for the first time associated the Grand Ancestor with the southern suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 魏主命群臣議行次。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler ordered the ministers to discuss the dynastic succession in the cycle of the Five Virtues.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei ruler ordered his ministers to debate the dynasty's place in the cycle of the Five Virtues.

sentences.zh: 中書監高閭議，以為：「帝王莫不以中原為正統，不以世數為與奪，善惡為是非。

translations.literal: Supervisor of the Secretariat Gao Lu argued, holding: "Emperors and kings all take the Central Plains as orthodoxy; they do not use the number of generations for gain or loss, nor good and evil for right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor of the Secretariat Gao Lu argued that "emperors and kings all took the Central Plains as the seat of orthodoxy and did not use the count of generations to decide succession, nor personal virtue or vice to determine legitimacy.

sentences.zh: 故桀、紂至虐，不廢夏、商之歷；

translations.literal: Thus though Jie and Zhou were utterly tyrannical, the calendars of Xia and Shang were not abolished;
translations.idiomatic: Thus even though Jie and Zhou were utterly tyrannical, the Xia and Shang dynasties were not struck from the succession;

sentences.zh: 厲、惠至昏，無害周、晉之錄。

translations.literal: though King Li and King Hui were utterly benighted, it did no harm to the records of Zhou and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: and even though King Li and King Hui were utterly benighted, the Zhou and Jin lines were not excluded from the record.

sentences.zh: 晉承魏為金，趙承晉為水，燕承趙為木，秦承燕為火。

translations.literal: Jin succeeded Wei as Metal; Zhao succeeded Jin as Water; Yan succeeded Zhao as Wood; Qin succeeded Yan as Fire.
translations.idiomatic: Jin had succeeded Wei as the Metal virtue; Zhao succeeded Jin as Water; Yan succeeded Zhao as Wood; and Qin succeeded Yan as Fire.

sentences.zh: 秦之既亡，魏乃稱制玄朔；

translations.literal: When Qin had perished, Wei then assumed rule over the dark north;
translations.idiomatic: When Qin fell, Wei assumed rule over the northern realm;

sentences.zh: 且魏之得姓，出於軒轅；

translations.literal: moreover, Wei received its surname from the Yellow Emperor;
translations.idiomatic: moreover, Wei traced its surname to the Yellow Emperor;

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為宜為土德。」

translations.literal: this subject, in his foolishness, holds that it should be Earth virtue."
translations.idiomatic: and in my humble view it ought to be assigned the Earth virtue."

sentences.zh: 秘書丞李彪、著作郎崔光等議，以為：「神元與晉武往來通好，至於桓、穆，志輔晉室，是則司馬祚終於郟鄏，而拓跋受命於雲代。

translations.literal: Secretary Director Li Biao, Compiler Cui Guang, and others argued, holding: "Shen Yuan exchanged friendly missions with Jin Emperor Wu; down to Huan and Mu, his purpose was to assist the Jin house—thus the Sima line ended at Jia and Luo, while the Tuoba received the mandate at Yun and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Secretary Director Li Biao, Compiler Cui Guang, and others argued that "Shen Yuan had exchanged friendly missions with Jin Emperor Wu, and down through Huan and Mu had sought to assist the Jin house. The Sima line had ended at Jia and Luo, while the Tuoba received the mandate at Yun and Dai.

sentences.zh: 昔秦並天下，漢猶比之共工，卒繼周為火德；

translations.literal: Formerly Qin united the realm, yet Han still compared it to Gong Gong and in the end succeeded Zhou as Fire virtue;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Qin had united the realm, yet Han still compared it to Gong Gong and in the end succeeded Zhou as the Fire virtue;

sentences.zh: 況劉、石、苻氏，地褊世促，魏承其弊，豈可捨晉而為土邪？」

translations.literal: how much more so the Liu, Shi, and Fu clans, whose territory was narrow and whose age was brief—Wei succeeded their decline; how can it abandon Jin and become Earth?"
translations.idiomatic: how much more so when the Liu, Shi, and Fu regimes held narrow territory and brief reigns, and Wei succeeded their decline. How can Wei abandon Jin and claim Earth instead?"

sentences.zh: 司空穆亮等皆請從彪等議。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Mu Liang and others all asked to follow the proposal of Biao and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Mu Liang and the others all asked to follow the proposal of Biao and his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，詔承晉為水德，神申、臘辰。

translations.literal: On renxu, an edict declared succession from Jin as Water virtue, with spirit-sacrifice on shen and winter sacrifice on chen.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renxu, an edict declared that Wei would succeed Jin as the Water virtue, with spirit-sacrifice on the day shen and winter sacrifice on the day chen.

sentences.zh: 甲子，魏罷租課。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Wei abolished rent assessment.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiazi, Wei abolished rent assessment.

sentences.zh: 魏宗室及功臣子孫封王者眾，乙丑，詔：「自非烈祖之冑，餘王皆降為公，公降為候，而品如舊。」

translations.literal: Among Wei imperial clansmen and descendants of meritorious ministers, many had been enfeoffed as kings. On yichou, an edict stated: "Except for descendants of the Illustrious Ancestor, all other kings are reduced to dukes, and dukes to marquises, while their ranks remain as before."
translations.idiomatic: Many members of the Wei imperial clan and descendants of meritorious ministers had been enfeoffed as kings. On the day yichou, an edict declared, "Except for descendants of the Illustrious Ancestor, all other kings are to be reduced to dukes, and dukes to marquises, while their official ranks remain unchanged."

sentences.zh: 蠻王桓誕亦降為公；

translations.literal: The barbarian king Huan Dan was also reduced to duke;
translations.idiomatic: The barbarian king Huan Dan was also reduced to duke;

sentences.zh: 唯上黨王長孫觀，以其祖有大功，特不降。

translations.literal: only Zhangsun Guan, Prince of Shangdang, because his grandfather had great merit, was specially not reduced.
translations.idiomatic: only Zhangsun Guan, Prince of Shangdang, was exempted because his grandfather had rendered great service.

sentences.zh: 丹陽王劉昶封齊郡公，加號宋王。

translations.literal: Liu Chang, Prince of Danyang, was enfeoffed as Duke of Qijun and given the additional title Prince of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chang, Prince of Danyang, was enfeoffed as Duke of Qijun and given the additional title Prince of Song.

sentences.zh: 魏舊制，四晨祭廟皆用中節，丙子，始詔用孟月，擇日而祭。

translations.literal: Under the old Wei system, the four seasonal dawn sacrifices at the ancestral temple all used the middle month of the season; on bingzi, an edict first ordered use of the first month of the season, choosing a day for sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old Wei system, the four seasonal dawn sacrifices at the ancestral temple had all been held in the middle month of each season. On the day bingzi, an edict ordered that they be held instead in the first month of each season, on a day chosen for the occasion.

sentences.zh: 以竟陵王子良領尚書令。

translations.literal: Prince Ziliang of Jingling was put in charge of the post of director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ziliang of Jingling was appointed director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 魏主毀太華殿，為太極殿。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler demolished Taihua Hall and built Taiji Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei ruler demolished Taihua Hall and built Taiji Hall in its place.

sentences.zh: 二月，戊子，徙居永樂宮。

translations.literal: In the second month, on wuzi, he moved his residence to Yongle Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day wuzi, he moved his residence to Yongle Palace.

sentences.zh: 以尚書李沖領將作大匠，與司空穆亮共營之。

translations.literal: Minister Li Chong was put in charge of the post of grand master of works and, together with Minister of Works Mu Liang, jointly oversaw construction.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Li Chong was appointed grand master of works and, together with Minister of Works Mu Liang, oversaw the construction.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，魏罷寒食鄉饗。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Wei abolished the Cold Food Festival village feast.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinmao, Wei abolished the village feast held at the Cold Food Festival.

sentences.zh: 甲午，魏主始朝日於東郊。

translations.literal: On jiawu, the Wei ruler for the first time performed the rite of greeting the sun at the eastern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiawu, the Wei ruler for the first time performed the rite of greeting the sun at the eastern suburb.

sentences.zh: 自是朝日、夕月皆親之。

translations.literal: From this, greeting the sun and saluting the moon he personally performed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he personally performed both the rites of greeting the sun and saluting the moon.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，詔祀堯於平陽，舜於廣寧，禹於安邑，周公於洛陽，皆令牧守執事；

translations.literal: On dingyou, an edict ordered sacrifice to Yao at Pingyang, to Shun at Guangning, to Yu at Anyi, and to the Duke of Zhou at Luoyang, all commanding governors and prefects to perform the rites;
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingyou, an edict ordered sacrifices to Yao at Pingyang, Shun at Guangning, Yu at Anyi, and the Duke of Zhou at Luoyang, commanding the local governors and prefects to perform the rites;

sentences.zh: 其宣尼之廟，祀於中書省。

translations.literal: the temple of Confucius was to be sacrificed to at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: while the temple of Confucius was to be honored with sacrifice at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 丁未，改謚宣尼曰文聖尼父，帝親行拜祭。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Confucius's posthumous title was changed to Cultured Sage, Master Ni; the emperor personally performed bowing sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingwei, Confucius's posthumous title was changed to Cultured Sage, Master Ni, and the emperor personally performed the bowing sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 魏舊制，氣歲祀天於西郊，魏主與公卿從二千餘騎，戎服繞壇，謂之翕壇。

translations.literal: Under the old Wei system, at the seasonal turn of the year Heaven was sacrificed to at the western suburb; the Wei ruler and the dukes and ministers, with more than two thousand mounted followers, in military dress circled the altar—this was called "gathering at the altar."
translations.idiomatic: Under the old Wei system, at the turn of the season Heaven was sacrificed to at the western suburb. The Wei ruler and the dukes and ministers, with more than two thousand mounted followers in military dress, would circle the altar in what was called "gathering at the altar."

sentences.zh: 明日，復戎服登壇致祀，已又繞壇，謂之繞天。

translations.literal: The next day, again in military dress they ascended the altar to perform sacrifice, and afterward again circled the altar—this was called "circling Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The next day they would again ascend the altar in military dress to perform the sacrifice, and afterward circle it once more in what was called "circling Heaven."

sentences.zh: 三月，癸酉，詔盡省之。

translations.literal: In the third month, on guiyou, an edict ordered all of this abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day guiyou, an edict abolished all of these practices.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，魏以高麗五雲為督遼海渚軍事、遼松公、高句麗王，詔雲遣其世子入朝。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Wei made Gouyun of Goguryeo commander of all military affairs on the islets of the Liao Sea, Duke of Liaosong, and King of Goguryeo, and ordered Gouyun to send his heir to court.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinsi, Wei appointed Gouyun of Goguryeo commander of all military affairs on the islets of the Liao Sea, Duke of Liaosong, and king of Goguryeo, and ordered him to send his heir to court.

sentences.zh: 雲辭以疾，遣其從叔升於隨使者詣平城。

translations.literal: Gouyun pleaded illness and sent his younger uncle Sheng Yu to follow the envoys to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Gouyun pleaded illness and sent his younger uncle Sheng Yu to accompany the envoys to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丁亥朔，魏班新律令，大赦。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the first day dinghai, Wei promulgated the new statutes and ordinances and granted a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the new moon of dinghai, Wei promulgated the new statutes and ordinances and declared a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，豫章文獻王嶷卒，贈假黃鉞、都督中外諸軍事、丞相，喪禮皆如漢東平獻王故事。

translations.literal: On xinchou, Prince Wenxian of Yuzhang, Xiao Yi, died; he was posthumously granted the yellow battle-axe, command of all military affairs within and without, and the post of chancellor; funeral rites all followed the precedent of the Han Prince Xian of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinchou, Xiao Yi, Prince Wenxian of Yuzhang, died. He was posthumously granted the yellow battle-axe, command of all military affairs within and without, and the post of chancellor, and his funeral rites followed the precedent set for the Han Prince Xian of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 嶷性仁謹廉儉，不以財賄為事。

translations.literal: Yi's nature was benevolent, careful, incorrupt, and frugal; he did not make bribery his business.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was benevolent, careful, incorrupt, and frugal, and never engaged in bribery.

sentences.zh: 齋庫失火，燒荊州還資，評直三千餘萬，主局各杖數十而已。

translations.literal: The fast-day storehouse caught fire and burned the returned goods from Jingzhou, assessed at more than thirty million; the heads of the offices were each flogged several dozen strokes, and that was all.
translations.idiomatic: When the fast-day storehouse caught fire and burned the goods returned from Jingzhou, assessed at more than thirty million, the heads of the responsible offices were each flogged several dozen strokes and nothing more.

sentences.zh: 疾篤，遺令諸子曰：「才有優劣，位有通塞，運有貧富，此自然之理，無足以相陵侮也。」

translations.literal: When his illness was grave, he left instructions to his sons, saying, "Talent has high and low; office has success and obstruction; fortune has poverty and wealth—this is the natural order, and nothing in it suffices for mutual bullying."
translations.idiomatic: When his illness grew grave, he left instructions to his sons: "Talent has its degrees, office its advances and setbacks, and fortune its poverty and wealth. These are natural conditions and give no one grounds to bully another."

sentences.zh: 上哀痛特甚，久之，語及嶷，猶歔欷流涕。

translations.literal: The emperor grieved with exceptional pain; long afterward, whenever he spoke of Yi, he still sobbed and shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved deeply. Long afterward, whenever he spoke of Yi, he still sobbed and shed tears.

sentences.zh: 嶷卒之日，第庫無見錢，上敕月給嶷第錢百萬；

translations.literal: On the day Yi died, the treasury of his residence had no cash on hand; the emperor ordered a monthly allowance of one million to Yi's household;
translations.idiomatic: On the day Yi died, his household treasury held no cash on hand, so the emperor ordered that his residence be granted one million cash each month;

sentences.zh: 終上之世乃省。

translations.literal: only at the end of the emperor's reign was it discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: and this allowance continued until the end of the emperor's reign.

sentences.zh: 五月，己巳，以竟陵王子良為揚州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on jisi, Prince Ziliang of Jingling was made governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the day jisi, Prince Ziliang of Jingling was appointed governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 魏文明太后之喪，使人告於吐谷渾。

translations.literal: At the mourning for Empress Dowager Wenming of Wei, envoys were sent to announce it to Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Wenming of Wei died, envoys were sent to announce her mourning to Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾王伏連籌拜命不恭，群臣請討之，魏主不許；

translations.literal: Foulianchou, king of Tuyuhun, received the command without proper respect; the ministers asked to punish him, but the Wei ruler would not allow it;
translations.idiomatic: Foulianchou, king of Tuyuhun, received the announcement without proper respect. His ministers asked to punish him, but the Wei ruler refused;

sentences.zh: 又請還其貢物，帝曰：「貢物乃人臣之禮。

translations.literal: they again asked to return his tribute goods; the emperor said, "Tribute goods are the ritual of a subject.
translations.idiomatic: they again asked to return his tribute. The emperor said, "Tribute is the proper ritual of a subject.

sentences.zh: 今而不受，是棄絕之，彼雖欲自新，其路無由矣。」

translations.literal: If now we do not accept them, that is to cast him off; though he may wish to reform himself, he will have no way to do so."
translations.idiomatic: If we refuse them now, we cast him off entirely. Even if he wishes to reform himself, he will have no way to do so."

sentences.zh: 因命歸洮陽、泥和之俘。

translations.literal: He therefore ordered the return of captives from Taoyang and Nihe.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore ordered the return of captives taken at Taoyang and Nihe.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，庚申，吐谷渾遣其世子賀虜頭入朝於魏。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on gengshen, Tuyuhun sent its heir Helutou to court at Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day gengshen, Tuyuhun sent its heir Helutou to court at Wei.

sentences.zh: 詔以伏連籌為都督西垂諸軍事、西海公、吐谷渾王，遣兼員外散騎常侍張禮使於吐谷渾。

translations.literal: An edict made Foulianchou commander of all military affairs in the western marches, Duke of Xihai, and King of Tuyuhun, and sent Acting Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary Zhang Li as envoy to Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Foulianchou commander of all military affairs in the western marches, Duke of Xihai, and king of Tuyuhun, and sent Acting Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary Zhang Li as envoy to Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 伏連籌謂禮曰：「曩者宕昌常自稱名而見謂為大王，今忽稱僕，又拘執使人；

translations.literal: Foulianchou said to Li, "Formerly Dangchang often called himself by name yet was addressed as Great King; now suddenly he is called Servant, and moreover envoys are seized and detained;
translations.idiomatic: Foulianchou said to Li, "Formerly Dangchang used to call himself by name yet was addressed as Great King. Now suddenly he is called Servant, and moreover our envoys are seized and detained;

sentences.zh: 欲使偏師往問，何如？」

translations.literal: I wish to send a detached force to inquire—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: I wish to send a detached force to demand an explanation. What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 禮曰：「君與宕昌皆為魏籓，比輒興兵攻之，殊違臣節。

translations.literal: Li said, "Your lordship and Dangchang are both vassals of Wei; to repeatedly raise troops and attack him grossly violates the duty of a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Li replied, "Your lordship and Dangchang are both vassals of Wei. To repeatedly raise troops and attack him grossly violates the duty of a subject.

sentences.zh: 離京師之日，宰輔有言，以為君能自知其過，則籓業可保；

translations.literal: On the day I left the capital, the chief ministers spoke, holding that if your lordship can know your own fault, then your vassal enterprise can be preserved;
translations.idiomatic: On the day I left the capital, the chief ministers said that if your lordship can recognize your own fault, your vassal status can be preserved;

sentences.zh: 若其不悛，禍難將至矣。」

translations.literal: if you do not reform, disaster will soon arrive."
translations.idiomatic: but if you do not reform, disaster will soon follow."

sentences.zh: 伏連籌默然。

translations.literal: Foulianchou was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Foulianchou fell silent.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，魏遣兼員外散騎常侍廣平宋弁等來聘。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Wei sent Acting Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary Song Bian of Guangping and others on a mission of courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiaxu, Wei sent Acting Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary Song Bian of Guangping and others on a diplomatic mission.

sentences.zh: 及還，魏主問弁：「江南何如？」

translations.literal: When they returned, the Wei ruler asked Bian, "How is the region south of the Yangtze?"
translations.idiomatic: When they returned, the Wei ruler asked Bian, "What is the situation south of the Yangtze?"

sentences.zh: 弁曰：「蕭氏父子無大功於天下，既以逆取，不能順守；

translations.literal: Bian said, "The Xiao father and son have no great achievement for the realm; having seized power by rebellion, they cannot preserve it by obedience;
translations.idiomatic: Bian replied, "The Xiao father and son have rendered no great service to the realm. Having seized power by rebellion, they cannot preserve it through orderly rule;

sentences.zh: 政令苛碎，賦役繁重；

translations.literal: government orders are harsh and minute, taxes and corvée are heavy and numerous;
