translations.idiomatic: their government orders are harsh and minute, and taxes and corvée are heavy and burdensome;

sentences.zh: 朝無股肱之臣，野有愁怨之民。

translations.literal: in court there are no trunk-and-limb ministers, in the wilds there are grieving and resentful people;
translations.idiomatic: the court lacks loyal pillars of support, and in the countryside there are people full of grief and resentment;

sentences.zh: 其得沒身幸矣，非貽厥孫謀之道也。」

translations.literal: merely to obtain death in old age would be fortunate; this is not the way of leaving plans for one's descendants."
translations.idiomatic: they would be fortunate merely to die of natural causes; that is hardly the way to leave a legacy for their descendants."

sentences.zh: 八月，乙未，魏以懷朔鎮將陽平王頤、鎮北大將軍陸睿皆為都督，督十二將，步騎十萬，分為三道以擊柔然：中道出黑山，東道趣士盧河，西道趣侯延河。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on yimou, Wei made the general of Huashuo Garrison, the Prince of Yangping, Yi, and the General Who Guards the North, Lu Rui, both grand marshals, commanding twelve generals with one hundred thousand infantry and cavalry, divided into three columns to attack Rouran: the center column went out by Black Mountain, the eastern column aimed for the Shilu River, and the western column aimed for the Houyan River.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the day yimou, Northern Wei appointed Yi, Prince of Yangping and commander of Huashuo Garrison, and Lu Rui, general who guards the north, both as overall commanders over twelve generals and one hundred thousand infantry and cavalry. They split into three columns to attack the Rouran: the center column marched through Black Mountain, the eastern column toward the Shilu River, and the western column toward the Houyan River.

sentences.zh: 軍過大磧，大破柔然而還。

translations.literal: The army crossed the great desert, inflicted a great defeat on Rouran, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The army crossed the great desert, routed the Rouran, and returned.

sentences.zh: 初，柔然伏名敦可汗與其叔父那蓋，分道擊高車阿伏至羅，伏名敦屢敗，那蓋屢勝。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Rouran khan Fumidun and his uncle Nagai split their forces to attack Avuzhiluo of the Gaoche; Fumidun was repeatedly defeated, while Nagai repeatedly won.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Rouran khan Fumidun and his uncle Nagai had divided their forces to attack Avuzhiluo of the Gaoche. Fumidun suffered defeat again and again, while Nagai won victory after victory.

sentences.zh: 國人以那蓋為得天助，乃殺伏名敦而立那蓋，號候其伏代庫者可汗，改元大安。

translations.literal: The people of the state thought Nagai was aided by Heaven, so they killed Fumidun and enthroned Nagai, calling him Khan Huiqifudaike, and changed the era name to Da'an.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran believed Nagai enjoyed Heaven's favor, so they killed Fumidun and enthroned Nagai in his place, styling him Khan Huiqifudaike and changing the era name to Da'an.

sentences.zh: 魏司徒尉元、大鴻臚卿游明根累表請老，魏主許之。

translations.literal: Wei's Minister of Education Wei Yuan and Grand Master of Ceremonies You Minggen repeatedly memorialized requesting retirement; the Wei ruler granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's minister of education, Wei Yuan, and grand master of ceremonies, You Minggen, repeatedly memorialized asking to retire, and the Wei ruler approved.

sentences.zh: 引見，賜元玄冠、素衣，明根委貌、青紗單衣，及被服雜物等而遣之。

translations.literal: He summoned them for audience, granted Yuan a black cap and plain white garments, granted Minggen a wei-mao cap and a blue gauze unlined robe, along with clothing and miscellaneous accouterments, and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: He received them in audience and sent them off with gifts: for Yuan, a black cap and plain white robes; for Minggen, a wei-mao cap and a blue gauze unlined garment, along with other clothing and household items.

sentences.zh: 魏主親養三老、五更於明堂。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler personally provided for the Three Elders and Five Respected Ones in the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei ruler personally honored the Three Elders and Five Respected Ones in the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 己酉，詔以元為三老，明根為五更。

translations.literal: On jiyou, an edict appointed Yuan as Three Elders and Minggen as Five Respected Ones.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiyou, an edict named Yuan Three Elders and Minggen Five Respected Ones.

sentences.zh: 帝再拜三老，親袒割牲，執爵而饋；

translations.literal: The emperor bowed twice to the Three Elders, personally bared his shoulder and cut the sacrificial victim, held the cup and presented the offering;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bowed twice to the Three Elders, bared his shoulder and cut the sacrificial animal himself, then held the cup and presented the offering;

sentences.zh: 肅拜五更；

translations.literal: he performed a respectful bow to the Five Respected Ones;
translations.idiomatic: he made a respectful bow to the Five Respected Ones;

sentences.zh: 且乞言焉，元、明根勸以孝友化民。

translations.literal: and then requested their counsel; Yuan and Minggen urged him to transform the people through filial piety and brotherly love.
translations.idiomatic: then asked for their counsel, and Yuan and Minggen urged him to transform the people through filial piety and brotherly affection.

sentences.zh: 又養國老、庶老於階下。

translations.literal: He also provided for the state elders and common elders below the steps.
translations.idiomatic: He also honored the state elders and common elders on the steps below.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，各賜元、明根以步挽車及衣服，祿三老以上公，五更以元卿。

translations.literal: When the rites were complete, he granted Yuan and Minggen each a hand-drawn carriage and clothing; the Three Elders received the stipend of a senior lord, and the Five Respected Ones that of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When the ceremony was finished, he gave Yuan and Minggen each a hand-drawn carriage and robes. The Three Elders received the emolument of a senior duke, and the Five Respected Ones that of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 九月，甲寅，魏主序昭穆於明堂，祀文明太后於玄室，辛未，魏主以文明太后再期，哭於永固陵左，終日不輟聲，凡二日不食。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on jiayin, the Wei ruler ordered the zhao-mu sequence in the Bright Hall and sacrificed to Empress Dowager Wenming in the Mysterious Chamber; on xinwei, as the second mourning period for Empress Dowager Wenming ended, the Wei ruler wept at the left of Yonggu Mausoleum without ceasing all day, and for two days took no food.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the day jiayin, the Wei ruler arranged the zhao-mu order in the Bright Hall and sacrificed to Empress Dowager Wenming in the Mysterious Chamber. On xinwei, when the second mourning period for Empress Dowager Wenming ended, the Wei ruler wept beside Yonggu Mausoleum without stopping all day and went without food for two days.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，辭陵，還永樂宮。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, he took leave of the tomb and returned to the Yongle Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiaxu, he took leave of the tomb and returned to the Yongle Palace.

sentences.zh: 武興氐王楊集始寇漢中，至白馬。

translations.literal: Yang Jishi, king of the Wuxing Di, raided Hanzhong and reached Baima.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jishi, king of the Wuxing Di, invaded Hanzhong and advanced as far as Baima.

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史陰智伯遣軍主桓盧奴、陰沖昌等擊破之，俘斬數千人。

translations.literal: The governor of Liang Province, Yin Zhibo, dispatched the commanders Huan Lunu, Yin Chongchang, and others, who routed them and captured or killed several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhibo, governor of Liang Province, sent the commanders Huan Lunu, Yin Chongchang, and others against them. They routed the invaders and captured or killed several thousand men.

sentences.zh: 集始走還武興，請降於魏；

translations.literal: Jishi fled back to Wuxing and requested surrender to Wei;
translations.idiomatic: Jishi fled back to Wuxing and submitted to Wei;

sentences.zh: 辛巳，入朝於魏。

translations.literal: On xinsi, he came to court in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinsi, he came to court in Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏以集始為南秦州刺史、漢中郡侯、武興王。

translations.literal: Wei appointed Jishi governor of South Qin Province, marquis of Hanzhong commandery, and king of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Wei appointed Jishi governor of South Qin Province, marquis of Hanzhong commandery, and king of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲午，上殷祭太廟。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jiawu, the Emperor performed the yin sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the day jiawu, the Emperor performed the yin sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，魏以安定王休為大司馬，特進馮誕為司徒。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Wei appointed the Prince of Anding, Xiu, Grand Marshal, and the specially advanced Feng Dan Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengxu, Wei appointed Xiu, Prince of Anding, grand marshal, and Feng Dan, specially advanced, minister of education.

sentences.zh: 誕，熙之子也。

translations.literal: Dan was a son of Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was a son of Xi.

sentences.zh: 魏太極殿成。

translations.literal: Wei's Hall of Supreme Ultimate was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei's Hall of Supreme Ultimate was completed.

sentences.zh: 十二月，司徒參軍蕭琛、范雲聘於魏。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the staff officer to the Minister of Education, Xiao Chen, and Fan Yun were sent on a diplomatic mission to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Xiao Chen, staff officer to the minister of education, and Fan Yun were sent on a diplomatic mission to Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏主甚重齊人，親與談論。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler held the men of Qi in great esteem and personally discussed with them.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei ruler held the Qi envoys in high regard and spoke with them personally.

sentences.zh: 顧謂群臣曰：「江南多好臣。」

translations.literal: Turning to his ministers he said, "There are many fine ministers south of the Yangtze."
translations.idiomatic: Turning to his ministers, he said, "There are many fine ministers south of the Yangtze."

sentences.zh: 侍臣李元凱對曰：「江南多好臣，歲一易主；

translations.literal: Attendant Li Yuankai replied, "There are many fine ministers south of the Yangtze—they change their lord every year;
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Li Yuankai replied, "There are indeed many fine ministers south of the Yangtze—they change their lord every year;

sentences.zh: 江北無好臣，百年一易主。」

translations.literal: north of the Yangtze there are no fine ministers, yet rulers change only once in a hundred years."
translations.idiomatic: north of the Yangtze there are no fine ministers, yet rulers change only once in a century."

sentences.zh: 魏主甚慚。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei ruler was deeply shamed.

sentences.zh: 上使太子家令沈約撰《宋書》，疑立《袁粲傳》，審之於上。

translations.literal: The Emperor had the heir apparent's steward Shen Yue compile the Book of Song; uncertain whether to include a biography of Yuan Can, he sought the Emperor's judgement.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had Shen Yue, steward to the heir apparent, compile the Book of Song. Uncertain whether to include a biography of Yuan Can, Shen Yue sought the Emperor's judgement.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「袁粲自是宋室忠臣。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Yuan Can was by nature a loyal minister of the Song house."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Yuan Can was truly a loyal minister of the Song house."

sentences.zh: 約又多載宋世祖、太宗諸鄙瀆事。

translations.literal: Shen Yue also included many indecent affairs of Emperor Xiaowu and Emperor Ming of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yue also included many indecent episodes concerning Emperor Xiaowu and Emperor Ming of Song.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「孝武事跡，不容頓爾。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "The deeds of Emperor Xiaowu cannot all be set down at once like this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "The deeds of Emperor Xiaowu cannot all be recorded so bluntly at once.

sentences.zh: 我昔經事明帝，卿可思諱惡之義。」

translations.literal: I once served Emperor Ming; you should reflect on the meaning of concealing evil."
translations.idiomatic: I once served Emperor Ming myself; you should reflect on the principle of concealing a ruler's faults."

sentences.zh: 於是多所刪除。

translations.literal: As a result, much was deleted.
translations.idiomatic: As a result, much was deleted.

sentences.zh: 是歲，林邑王范陽邁之孫諸農，帥種人攻范當根純，復得其國。

translations.literal: That year, Zhunong, grandson of Fan Yangmai, king of Linyi, led tribesmen to attack Fan Dangenchun and recovered the kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Zhunong, grandson of Fan Yangmai, king of Linyi, led his tribesmen against Fan Dangenchun and recovered the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 詔以諸農為都督緣海諸軍事、林邑王。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Zhunong commander-in-chief of all coastal military affairs and king of Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Zhunong commander-in-chief of all coastal military affairs and king of Linyi.

sentences.zh: 魏南陽公鄭羲與李沖婚姻，沖引為中書令。

translations.literal: Zheng Xi, Duke of Nanyang of Wei, was related by marriage to Li Chong, who brought him in as Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xi, Duke of Nanyang of Wei, was related by marriage to Li Chong, who brought him in as director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 出為西兗州刺史，在州貪鄙。

translations.literal: When sent out as governor of West Yan Province, he was greedy and base in office.
translations.idiomatic: When sent out as governor of West Yan Province, he proved greedy and corrupt in office.

sentences.zh: 文明太后為魏主納其女為嬪，征為秘書監。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming had the Wei ruler take his daughter as a consort and summoned Xi to serve as Director of the Library.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming had the Wei ruler take his daughter as a consort and summoned Xi back to serve as director of the library.

sentences.zh: 及卒，尚書奏謚曰宣。

translations.literal: When he died, the Ministry of Works memorialized that his posthumous name should be Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, the Ministry of Works memorialized that his posthumous name should be Xuan.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「蓋棺定謚，激揚清濁。

translations.literal: An edict said, "Once the lid is on the coffin the posthumous name is fixed, to exalt the pure and reprove the foul.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Once the coffin is closed the posthumous name is fixed, to exalt the upright and condemn the corrupt.

sentences.zh: 故何曾雖孝，良史載其繆丑；

translations.literal: Thus though He Zeng was filial, good historians recorded his errors and disgrace;
translations.idiomatic: Thus though He Zeng was filial, good historians recorded his errors and disgrace;

sentences.zh: 賈充有勞，直士謂之荒公。

translations.literal: though Jia Chong had merit, upright men called him Duke Huang.
translations.idiomatic: though Jia Chong had merit, upright men called him Duke Absurd.

sentences.zh: 羲雖宿有文業，而治闕廉清。

translations.literal: Though Xi had long-standing literary attainments, his governance lacked integrity and purity.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xi had long-standing literary attainments, his governance lacked integrity and purity.

sentences.zh: 尚書何乃情遺至公，愆違明典！

translations.literal: How could the Ministry of Works so emotionally depart from utmost fairness and violate the clear statutes!
translations.idiomatic: How could the Ministry of Works so far depart from utmost fairness in its partiality and violate the clear statutes!

sentences.zh: 依《謚法》：『博聞多見曰文，不勤成名曰靈。』

translations.literal: According to the Posthumous Name Law: 'Broadly learned and widely seen is called Wen; attaining renown without diligence is called Ling.'
translations.idiomatic: According to the Posthumous Name Law: 'Broadly learned and widely seen is called Wen; attaining renown without diligence is called Ling.'

sentences.zh: 可贈以本官，加謚文靈。」

translations.literal: He may be granted his former office and given the additional posthumous name Wen Ling."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be granted his former office and given the additional posthumous name Wen Ling."
